```
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
data/        this repository's own transcripts, runs, knowledge packs (see data/README.md)
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and residue of deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns it
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when required content genuinely needs the space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via its sync procedure; re-apply or retire logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

</system-reminder>

21:  datasets/<name>/                                          one fold of every record's trajectories into train.jsonl, heldout.jsonl, and a manifest of the counts, distributions, digests, and the data-use purpose it was filtered for (see its own README)
52:Every record here ran its cells in a sibling layout — each cell workspace directly under the run directory, beside `plan.json`, the run log, and every other cell of the same fleet — and the records dated 2026-09-08 and earlier ran them unconfined, so nothing stopped a cell from reading any of it. [`tools/census-escapes.mjs`](tools/census-escapes.mjs) reads one record and reports, per cell, the tool calls whose path arguments name the run directory or another cell and the reads the barrier refused; [`tools/record-run.mjs`](tools/record-run.mjs) prints that census, and the per-arm totals below, with every record it writes; a run whose driver died before writing its result is recorded with `--partial <reason>`, which keeps its session logs, states only the reason in its `result.json`, and leaves any verdict to an offline fold under `folds/`. [`tools/summarize-run.mjs`](tools/summarize-run.mjs) reads one record the same way, or a run directory a driver is still writing, and prints, per cell, the arm, the implementer and route, the certificate, the attempts, the wall seconds, the steps, and the usage (a delegated cell's from its delegation records, as the runner reports it), then one line of totals per arm; the certificate counts, attempts, and usage the paragraphs below state are read from it. [`tools/build-dashboard.mjs`](tools/build-dashboard.mjs) folds every record and fold into [`dashboard.html`](dashboard.html), one self-contained page: the verdict of every paired comparison with its interval, the product models on sealed tier 5, the certification rate of every environment under every route, when each record ran, one row per record opening onto its cells and its paragraph here, the routing and repeatability readings, and one row per `bench loop` iteration once `loop/ledger.jsonl` exists; `--live <run dir>` adds a run a driver is still writing. [`improvement-log.md`](improvement-log.md) is the hand-written ledger over the same records and folds, one row per improvement iteration: the change proposed, what tested it, the paired reading, and the decision taken. [`tools/build-dataset.mjs`](tools/build-dataset.mjs) reads every record at once rather than one, folding their trajectories into a dataset under `datasets/<name>/` and refusing to write anything while any trajectory carries a credential- or mailbox-shaped string; `--purpose <delivery|training|evaluation>` keeps only the trajectories whose own `terms` admit that purpose and counts the rest as `withheldTerms`, so a training set is built with `--purpose training`, and a trajectory carrying no terms admits no purpose and is withheld. Over this corpus the census finds cells that left their own workspace in ten records: 4 of 12 in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t2`, 11 of 18 in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t4`, 3 of 36 in `2026-09-07-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t3`, 8 of 36 in `2026-09-08-bench-e1-haiku-vs-sonnet-t3`, 7 of 36 in `2026-09-08-bench-e1-sonnet-vs-opus-t3`, 6 of 32 in `2026-09-08-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t5`, 7 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e3-attempts1-t3`, 3 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e3-baseline-t3`, 15 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e4-knowledge-pack-t3`, and 9 of 16 in `2026-09-08-bench-h1-harness-loop-t5`; the other eight records count none, seven of them because every cell was delegated to the product, where the harness session holds no tool call of its own and the census can see nothing the delegate did, and the eighth because it is a one-cell smoke. Two escapes changed what a row measures: in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t2` the `code:csv-codec` cell `cell-cUuWY2` ran `cp cell-cUuWY2/src/csv.js cell-R8QtdK/src/csv.js`, putting its own solution into the other repetition of its task, and in `2026-09-08-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t5` the first `code:sheet-eval` cell `cell-Cr3CtN` wrote its whole solution into the second cell's workspace, `cell-XNKQXT`. A record made under a composition that confines its cells — where the runner denies each cell everything above its own workspace for the length of its run — carries the refusals as `escapesDenied` on every scoreboard and observatory row, so the count is read from the row rather than reconstructed from the log.
68:The same bench runs on an open-weight route through the `with-deepseek` overlay, which composes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek` beside the base's product route: export `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the launching shell and add `--overlay with-deepseek` to a plan whose arms name `deepseek-official` (`h1-fleet-deepseek-t2` as a fleet, `e8-deepseek-vs-sonnet-t3` as a frozen pair against `sonnet`). Without that variable the fleet refuses the plan before its first cell and names the credential, so a keyless attempt costs nothing and reports why. This matters beyond portability: every record above was produced on the operator's Claude Code subscription, whose terms admit its transcripts as evaluation only, so none of this corpus may enter [the RLVR datasets](datasets/): `--purpose training` withholds every one of its trajectories, and a run on a route whose data-use terms allow training is the only kind it would not withhold. The `with-openrouter` overlay is that route: it composes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` over OpenRouter's free tier with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` exported in the launching shell, pins terms that admit training under their own agreement id, and its records of 2026-09-19 (the thirty-fourth and thirty-fifth above) are the first cells on another route — six cells, none certified, so the corpus a training dataset would admit still holds no certificate.

The twenty-second record is the eighteenth rerun as the slate meant it: the harness loop as the baseline arm against the product's own loop as the candidate, the same middle model on both, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 7,235 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition with session continuity on the route and, for the first time, the same caps on both arms: 1,500,000 billed tokens (input plus cache read plus cache write, as the budget policy bills every route) and 1,200,000 ms of wall time per cell, applied to a delegated attempt as to the harness's own. The harness loop certified 15 of 16 (14 at the first attempt, conf-canon once at the third, sheet-eval missed once after three attempts); the product loop 14 of 16, every one at its first attempt, delta −0.0625, interval [−0.125, 0], verdict inconclusive, and the delta is one flip, inside the noise floor the twenty-first record measured. What the parity changed is visible in the two product misses: lex-states breached the token cap after one attempt (1,786,072 billed tokens measured against 1,500,000) and sheet-eval the wall cap (1,202,455 ms against 1,200,000), so neither got the second attempt the eighteenth record's uncapped product arm took, and the cell the product loop had recovered there was not recovered here. Under the same caps the harness loop was the faster arm in 15 of 16 pairs, 5,740 s of cell time against 8,187 (medians 255 s against 422), and the cheaper one: 447,289 output tokens and 7,695,132 billed tokens against 625,239 output and 25,817,220 billed on the product side, where the product reported 14.72 USD for its fifteen attempts that reported usage at all. Three of the harness loop's sealed runs on these cells now stand at 15, 14, and 13 of 16, one or two flips apart; the product loop's two runs at 14 and 11, the second of them uncapped and unsealed. Read with the eighth record and the tier-2 and tier-4 fleets, the harness loop is never worse than the product loop on certificates and is faster at tier 2 and tier 5, slower at tier 4, and the difference it makes is not in certificates but in what surrounds them: the caps hold, the record is complete, and the cell is sealed. The census finds seven harness cells naming their parent or the run directory in eight tool calls, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied; the product's child runs outside the harness log, so its own calls are not censused.

The twenty-first record is the sealed tier-5 form of the thirteenth: the middle product model as the baseline arm against the smallest as the candidate, on the harness loop, over the same eight audited environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 8,883 s of wall time at two cells at a time, under the confined composition of the twentieth (both experiments were relaunched together at 10:47 UTC on `32a2cac6a`, which is the commit their rows name; the twentieth's rows had named the head at record time and were corrected). The middle model certified 14 of 16 (9 at the first attempt, five at the second, sheet-eval missed twice after three attempts); the smallest certified 1 of 16, ranked-choice once at the first attempt, and spent all three attempts on every other cell, delta −0.8125, interval [−0.875, −0.75], verdict reject: at tier 5 the smallest model is not an implementer for these tasks, where at tier 3 it was level on certificates. It was also the most expensive arm on record: 604 model steps against 262, 11,227 s of cell time against 6,337 (median 725 s against 297), 736,856 output tokens against 481,591, 1,077,050 cache-write tokens against 669,507 and 21,275,855 cache-read against 7,633,594, because a cell that fails three times rereads its growing transcript three times over. Read with the twentieth record, the three product models order strictly on every cell: no cell the smallest certified was missed by the middle one, and none the middle one certified was missed by the largest, so the offline routing reading over the three single-model arms ([folds/2026-09-08-routing-t5-seed2.json](folds/2026-09-08-routing-t5-seed2.json)) is exact rather than estimated. The oracle that picks the cheapest certifying model per cell is the largest model alone (16 of 16, 189,169 output tokens, 164 steps, 3,572 s), and so is the strong-first cascade; the cheap-first cascade over all three reaches 16 of 16 at 1,248,222 output tokens and 18,028 s, 6.6 and 5.0 times the largest model alone; the middle-then-largest cascade at 525,564 tokens and 7,006 s, 2.8 and 2.0 times. Every cascade that starts below the largest model pays the smaller model's whole failure before it escalates, so on this bench the routing question is not which model to try first but whether a hard cell can be told apart before any model runs, and nothing in the stamp tells it apart. The three runs of the middle model on these cells also give the bench its noise floor ([folds/2026-09-08-sonnet-repeatability-t5-seed2.json](folds/2026-09-08-sonnet-repeatability-t5-seed2.json)): the two sealed runs (this record and the twentieth) agree on 15 of 16 cells, one flip; each agrees with the unsealed eighteenth on 14 and 13 of 16, where conf-canon certified twice in both sealed runs and never in the unsealed one. A paired delta of 0.0625 on sixteen cells is therefore within one arm's own run-to-run variation, and the twentieth's 0.1875 is three times it. The census finds seven cells naming their parent or the run directory in twelve tool calls; every such call saw the empty sealed directory, and no read was denied.

The twentieth record is the first frozen paired experiment on the sealed bench and the first whose interval excludes zero: the middle product model as the baseline arm against the largest as the candidate, on the harness loop, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,742 s of wall time at two cells at a time, under the composition that confines every cell with bwrap (a cell's parent directory is an empty tmpfs holding only the cell), resumes one product session per harness session, and forwards each hidden case's arguments through the reserved check script. The largest model certified 16 of 16 at the first attempt; the middle one 13 of 16 (11 at the first attempt, diff3-merge and rate-limit-sim once each at the second, sheet-eval missed twice at the 1,200,000 ms wall cap and lex-states once after three attempts), delta 0.1875, interval [0.125, 0.25], verdict promote at the 0.05 minimum delta: on these tasks the largest model is the better implementer, and the difference sits where the specification has corners the middle model does not reach in three attempts. The largest model was also the cheaper and faster arm on every measure: 164 model steps against 267, 3,572 s of cell time against 7,451 (median 204 s against 387), 189,169 output tokens against 561,271, and with session continuity now on the route the spend is read-dominant, 2,185,841 cache-read against 317,394 cache-write tokens for the candidate and 8,515,603 against 738,281 for the baseline, where the eighteenth record's harness loop wrote 2,927,150 and read 626,621. The census finds seven cells that named the run directory or their parent in eight tool calls; under the seal every such call saw an empty directory holding only the cell's own workspace, as the recorded results show, and no read was denied because nothing reachable was denied. This is the first promotion-level verdict of the program and it promotes a model, not a change to the harness; read with the thirteenth and fourteenth records it says the model tiers separate on certificates at tier 5 where tier 3 saturated, and it says nothing yet about the harness loop against the product loop, whose sealed rerun follows.

The nineteenth record is the harness assessing itself through its own program workflow: one department on the route, the largest product model, reading an eleven-file evidence dossier in its worktree (this README, the census, the record index, the last thirty hours of commits, the slate, the roles matrix, the sealed-cell note, the ruflo and baselines comparisons, and the question with the four goals) and writing `assessment.md`, certified by a committed verifier that requires four named sections, two verdict lines, at least eight evidence bullets each citing a dossier file that exists, six distinct files, and 600 to 2,500 words; the integration re-ran the verifier on the merged head. The department certified at its first validation after eleven steps (14 evidence bullets, 9 files cited, 2,258 words) with `Viable: undetermined (medium confidence)` and `State of the art: in part (medium confidence)`, the part being the measurement instrument and its enforcement rather than any measured capability; it also found that this lab's own summary table carries no contamination column and that the tier 2 to 4 comparisons are folds of separate fleets, not frozen experiments. The run exposed three defects in the program workflow, all kept in the artefacts directory beside the record ([2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json](2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json)): the department certified with the file written but never committed, so the integration merged an empty branch and failed on `missing assessment.md`; the integration agent, unconfined, then found the department's worktree and rewrote sentences of the certified file with a script before the operator stopped it after 22 steps; and the resume refused to republish the integration session's identity, so the operator committed the department tree as it then stood, set the first integration session aside, and resumed, after which the integration certified the merged head and the program released. The text the department certified is reconstructed byte for byte from its own session's write (`assessment.certified.md`, 2,258 words) and differs from the merged text in five lines, none of them a verdict.

The eighteenth record is the fourth frozen paired experiment and the tier-5 form of the eighth: the harness loop as the baseline arm against the product loop as the candidate arm, the same product model on both sides, on the eight tier-5 environments as audited (the conf-canon reference and six of its cases regenerated, the lex-states and sheet-eval prompts clarified), seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 8,979 s of wall time at two cells at a time. The harness loop certified 12 of 16 (9 at the first attempt, 3 at the second: diff3-merge, lex-states, and rate-limit-sim once each), the product loop 11 of 16 (10 at the first attempt and rate-limit-sim once at the second, the first recovery by a fresh child that received the directive alone), delta −0.0625, interval [−0.125, 0], verdict inconclusive. Three cells flip between the arms: the product loop certified conf-canon once where the harness loop never did, and the harness loop certified uri-resolve twice where the product loop's two cells failed three delegations each in 125 s with no reported model or cost, because they ran last, after 04:10 UTC, when the subscription's session limit had been reached (it reset at 05:30); on the 14 pairs the limit did not touch, the arms differ by one certificate in the product loop's favour. Both arms miss sheet-eval twice, the harness loop cut at the 1,200,000 ms wall cap and the product loop uncapped at 662 and 714 s, because in this run the composition's caps bound only the harness's own steps (the budget-parity slice landed after it). The product loop was the faster implementer, faster in 10 of 16 pairs, 7,554 s of cell time against 10,221, and reported 629,483 output tokens and 13.23 USD of list-price cost; the harness loop's 16 cells spent 802,872 output tokens, 626,621 cache-read and 2,927,150 cache-write tokens, with one transient route retry on each conf-canon cell that recovered. This record also carries the defect a census found after it: five of the harness loop's sixteen cells left their workspace for the run directory, read its plan and log and a sibling cell of their own environment (lex-states, rate-limit-sim, and conf-canon of the second repetition, and both sheet-eval cells), and the first sheet-eval cell did its work inside the second's workspace, while no product-loop cell left its own; the sealed-cell slice that denies a cell everything above its workspace is queued, and the tier-5 comparison is rerun under it before this verdict is read as more than what it is. Read with the eleventh and twelfth records, tier 5 does not separate the two loops on certificates either: both land at 11 or 12 of 16 on the same environments, with the misses on the same two tasks.

A counterfactual fold of the eleventh and twelfth records, written before the confirmatory pair at tier 5 runs, carries the attempt-cap hypothesis to the tier where attempts are taken ([folds/2026-09-08-attempts1-counterfactual-against-harness-loop-t5.json](folds/2026-09-08-attempts1-counterfactual-against-harness-loop-t5.json), [folds/2026-09-08-attempts1-counterfactual-against-product-loop-t5.json](folds/2026-09-08-attempts1-counterfactual-against-product-loop-t5.json)): each cell's outcome is replaced by the outcome of its first attempt alone, which is what the same run would have recorded under a cap of one attempt, since a first attempt cannot observe the attempts after it. On the harness loop the cap costs 3 of 11 certificates (`code:diff3-merge` twice and `code:lex-states` once, all recovered at the second attempt after a directive), delta −0.1875, interval [−0.25, −0.125], verdict reject for the capped candidate; on the product loop the cap costs nothing, delta 0, interval [0, 0], because none of its five failed cells recovered in a second or third attempt, and the delegation is why: a later attempt of a delegated cell starts a fresh child that receives the directive alone, without the task prompt or the earlier child's transcript, where a later attempt of the harness loop continues the same transcript with the task, its own work, and the directive in view. The two loops' later attempts are therefore not the same instrument, and the attempt-ladder slice that restates the task to a fresh child and names the transcript interface of every attempt is queued before the tier-5 rerun. The two intervals resample the 16 cells of one run each and carry no run-to-run variance, so they are narrower than a paired run's would be; the paired attempt-cap fleet on the audited tier-5 tasks is the confirmatory step, and until it lands this fold is evidence that the runner's directives convert failures on the harness loop and could not on the product loop as delegated today, not a promotion.

The seventeenth record is the knowledge-pack fold, the same nine tier-3 environments and two repetitions run with the composition overlay that serves the eight-theme 2026-q3 knowledge pack as the session's skill catalog, folded against the fifteenth record's baseline ([folds/2026-09-08-e4-knowledge-pack-against-baseline-t3.json](folds/2026-09-08-e4-knowledge-pack-against-baseline-t3.json)): 18 of 18 certified at the first attempt on both sides, delta 0, interval [0, 0]. The pack was never opened: the catalog of 2,778 characters stood in every request and no cell made a skill call, so this fold measures a catalog the model reads and ignores, not knowledge in use. The fleet's cells took 5,433 s against the baseline's 3,959 and 482,920 output tokens against 339,331, more than the four other sonnet tier-3 fleets on record (339,331 to 367,172); one fleet cannot say whether the catalog or run-to-run variance caused it. The hypothesis the pack was built to test, that task-relevant knowledge served as skills changes outcomes, needs a pack whose themes the tasks call for; this pack holds the research corpus, and these tasks do not call for it.

The fifteenth and sixteenth records are the first offline fold, the attempt-cap hypothesis: the same nine tier-3 environments and two repetitions run twice as fleets that differ only by the composition overlay that caps the runner at one attempt instead of three, then folded by the bench's fold driver into the same paired certificate-rate delta an experiment computes ([folds/2026-09-08-e3-attempts1-against-baseline-t3.json](folds/2026-09-08-e3-attempts1-against-baseline-t3.json)). Both fleets certified 18 of 18 at the first attempt, so the delta is 0 with interval [0, 0] and the fold says nothing about attempts: the baseline never used its second or third attempt, and a cap on attempts cannot show an effect where no attempt beyond the first is taken. The tier where attempts were taken is tier 5, where the eleventh record's harness loop certified three cells at the second attempt; the attempt-cap comparison belongs there and is queued behind the budget-parity slice.

The fourteenth record is the third frozen paired experiment, the largest product model as the candidate arm against the middle one, on the same nine tier-3 environments and the harness loop: 36 cells, 3,024 s of wall time. Both arms certified 18 of 18, so the verdict is inconclusive on certificates for the third time on this tier, and the baseline arm needed a second attempt on two cells this time where its earlier runs needed none, which is the run-to-run variance a paired design absorbs. The largest model was the cheaper implementer on every other measure: 156 model steps against 208, 2,070 s of cell time against 3,948 (median 118 s against 165), 166,606 output tokens against 367,172, and 2,071,448 cache-write tokens against 3,635,010. Across the thirteenth and fourteenth records the three product models order by spend, not by certificates: the largest spends the least on the harness loop because it takes the fewest steps, and every step of this route rewrites the prefix.

The thirteenth record is the second frozen paired experiment, the model-tier comparison on the harness loop: the same nine tier-3 environments, two repetitions, the smaller product model as the candidate arm against the middle one as the baseline, 36 cells, 5,437 s of wall time. Both arms certified 18 of 18 at the first attempt, so the delta is again 0 with interval [0, 0] and the verdict inconclusive: on certificates at this tier the smaller model is not worse. Everything else separates the tiers: the smaller model needed 405 model steps against 182, 6,719 s of cell time against 3,807 (its median cell 300 s against 207), 844,538 output tokens against 358,054, and 9,985,537 cache-write tokens against 3,070,990. Read with the eighth record, the bench's tier 3 is saturated on certificates for all three of these product models under both loops, and the differences between models and between loops live in steps, wall time, and spend.

The twelfth record is the product loop on the same eight tier-5 environments, the first delegated fleet whose cells carry the child's reported model, usage, and cost: sixteen cells, 11 certified, every certificate at the first attempt, 8,139 s of wall time at two cells at a time, 1,300,589 reported output tokens and 31.48 USD of reported list-price cost for the fleet. The certificates fall exactly where the harness loop's did in the eleventh record: the same six environments certified twice, lex-states once, conf-canon and sheet-eval never, and the misses stop at the same corners (conf-canon 144 of 150 on every attempt against the harness loop's 146, lex-states 158 of 160 against 159), which points at the specifications of those corners as much as at either implementer. The two implementers differ elsewhere: the product loop needed no second attempt where the harness loop needed three, its certified cells took 232 to 555 s against the harness loop's 150 to 599 s, and its misses ran uncapped for up to 3,459 s and 5.60 USD each because the composition's wall cap binds only the harness's own steps (the budget-parity slice is queued), where the harness loop's misses were cut at the 1,200,000 ms cap. The harness loop's 16 cells cost 860,596 output tokens against the product loop's 1,300,589, and 4,778,361 cache-write tokens against the product loop's read-dominant profile.

The eleventh record is the harness loop on tier 5, the tier judged on cases the implementer never sees: the eight tier-5 environments that are not held out, sixteen cells, 11 certified (8 at the first attempt, 3 at the second), 5,117 s of wall time at two cells at a time, 16.9 model steps per cell on average, 860,596 output tokens, 745,264 cache-read and 4,778,361 cache-write tokens. The tier separates: the five misses are two kinds. Three are specification corners the clustered directive did not lead the model to (conf-canon twice at 146 of 150 cases on every attempt, all four on the stderr channel; lex-states once at 159 of 160 on every attempt). Two are budget exhaustion: on sheet-eval the first attempt alone ran past the composition's 1,200,000 ms wall cap while writing very large modules, and on conf-canon the first attempt did the same after reaching 146 of 150, so the budget policy blocked the remaining attempts before the model could act on the directive. The route's per-step cost is visible in both kinds: every step is a fresh product session, and the two misses that breached the wall cap spent 12 and 35 steps on their first attempt.

The tenth record completes the harness loop's pass over tiers 2 to 4: the nine tier-4 environments, eighteen cells, every one certified in one attempt, 68 to 293 s per cell, median 175 s, 1467 s of wall time at two cells at a time, 13.2 model steps per cell on average, 214,397 output tokens, 655,134 cache-read and 4,024,446 cache-write tokens. On this tier the product loop was the faster implementer: set against the sixth record cell by cell, the harness loop was faster in 6 of 18 pairs and its cells took 2915 s in total against 2292 s. Tier 4 hands the implementer a module with planted defects, and the harness loop spends more short steps on it than on the other tiers; every step is a fresh product process that rewrites the whole prefix into the cache, which is where both the wall time and the cache-write tokens go. Across the three tiers both implementers certified 48 of 48 cells at one attempt each, the harness loop faster on tiers 2 and 3 and slower on tier 4.

The ninth record is the harness loop's fleet over the same six tier-2 environments the fourth record measured with the product loop: twelve cells, every one certified in one attempt, 37 to 481 s per cell, median 116 s, 979 s of wall time at two cells at a time, 7.6 model steps per cell on average, 158,899 output tokens, 255,502 cache-read and 884,168 cache-write tokens. Set beside the fourth record cell by cell (the same environment and repetition, in different fleets rather than one frozen plan), the harness loop was faster in 9 of 12 pairs and its cells took 1786 s in total against the product loop's 1932 s.

The eighth record is the first frozen paired experiment of the hypothesis program (digest `4c9659e3…`): the harness's own loop on the Claude Code route as the baseline arm against the product's own loop as the candidate arm, the same model on both sides, over the nine tier-3 environments that are not held out, two repetitions, seed 1, 36 cells, 4194 s of wall time at two cells at a time. Both arms certified 18 of 18 cells at one attempt each, so the certificate-rate delta is 0 with a bootstrap interval of [0, 0] and the verdict is inconclusive at the 0.05 minimum delta: on this tier the harness loop is neither better nor worse than the product loop on certificates, which refutes the hypothesis that the harness loop loses to the product loop on these tasks and does not support the hypothesis that it wins. Wall time is also level: the harness loop was faster in 11 of the 18 pairs, its median cell took 164 s against 179 s, and the two arms' totals differ by under one percent. The harness loop's spend is on record because its queries go through the harness: 352,494 output tokens and 553,676 cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3,005,288 cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session whose prefix is written to the cache again instead of read from it; the product loop keeps one session per cell and pays that once. The product arm's spend is not on this record: the slice that forwards the cell's model to the child and records the child's reported usage and cost merged after the run had started (the manifest's head carries it, the runs do not), so the next paired experiment carries both arms' spend.

The seventh record is the first cell the harness's own loop certified on the Claude Code route, immediately after the route began offering the harness tools natively: five model queries, five tool calls (explore, read the tests, read the stub, write the module, run the suite), no retry, one validation, 41 s from stamp to certificate, 2580 output tokens. The same environment took the product loop 59 and 63 s in the fourth record. Before that route change the same cell failed every query at the product's turn bound, which the route's note records.

The sixth record completes the product loop's pass over the bench: the nine tier-4 environments that are not held out, eighteen cells, every one certified in one attempt, 58 to 235 s per cell, 1151 s of wall time at two cells at a time. Tier 4 hands the implementer an existing module with planted defects and an immutable suite, which is why its cells are faster than tier 3's. Across the three fleets the product loop certified 48 of 48 cells at one attempt each, so on certificates this bench does not separate implementers at any tier for this product model; the bench's next slice is a harder tier and the six held-out environments, and every comparison below that reads attempts, wall time, and spend.

The fifth record is the same fleet plan on the nine tier-3 environments that are not held out: eighteen cells, every one certified in one attempt, 71 to 389 s per cell, 1844 s of wall time at two cells at a time. Tier 3 is therefore also a ceiling for the product loop on this bench, and a comparison that only counts certificates cannot separate implementers below tier 4; the separating measures at these tiers are attempts, wall time, and spend, of which the delegation record holds the first two and will hold the child's reported spend once the queued slice lands.

The fourth record is the Proving Ground bench's first fleet (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/`, thirty admitted program tasks): the product's own loop as the implementer of every cell, over the six tier-2 environments that are not held out, two repetitions each, seed 1, policy `bench-2026-09-07`, district `bench-h1`, two cells at a time, 984 s of wall time for the twelve cells. Every cell was certified in one attempt, so tier 2 is a ceiling for this implementer and the paired comparisons between the harness loop and the product loop run on tiers 3 and 4. The cells name the model `sonnet`; the product ran the installation's default model, which was measured as sonnet immediately before the run, because the delegation did not yet forward the cell's model to the child (the slice that forwards it and records the child's reported model is queued). The bench composition and tasks are those of commit `128e037bb`; the manifest records the head of the working tree at recording time.

The third record is the same district left running overnight: 22 slots on its thirty-minute cadence from 22:16 to 09:16 UTC, including the first slot the second record holds. The host restarted once; the slot due at 00:16 was not caught up, exactly as the shift driver's cadence rule states, and the relaunched process resumed the same ledger and cadence from 00:46 on the working tree of that moment, so the slots before the restart ran the tree at `88f6a1f2e` and the slots after it the tree at `38dd04165`, which the manifest records as the head. Every one of the 66 cells was certified in one attempt; the record holds all 22 shift ledgers, the 66 cell sessions, and the exports folded over them.

The second run is the live district's first slot after two defects the district itself exposed were fixed: a test check this Node rejected, and a runner that overlaid the whole fixture before validation and so discarded every edit to a fixture-supplied source file. Three program tasks, each with an immutable test suite, were implemented by the product in one attempt each and certified by the runner on the trees it left; the held-out task never entered the plan.

The first run is the first time an agent other than the harness itself was measured by the Proving Ground: two smoke environments at `isolation: none`, one child run per attempt recorded as `environment/delegation`, every delegation ending `completed`, facts exported for both sessions, both trajectories exported through the curator with one rewarded, and the observatory publishing both rows under the `claude-code` implementer with `runner` as the certificate executor of the certified one.

162	/**
163	 * Whether one e-mail match names a mailbox rather than a parser fixture.
164	 * @param {string} domain the address's mail domain
165	 * @returns {boolean} true when the domain could receive mail

167	function isMailboxDomain(domain) {
168	  if (RESERVED_EMAIL_DOMAIN_RE.test(domain)) return false
169	  const labels = domain.split('.')
170	  // A two-letter-or-shorter public suffix takes two labels (`x.co.uk`), so the registrable name sits one further left.
171	  const registrable = labels.length > 2 && labels.at(-2).length <= 3 ? labels.at(-3) : labels.at(-2)

175	/**
176	 * The matched text replaced by `[redacted]` inside a short window of its
177	 * string, so a refusal locates the hit without reprinting it.
178	 * @param {string} text the string the match was found in
179	 * @param {number} index where the match starts
180	 * @param {number} length how long the match is
181	 * @returns {string} a single-line excerpt
182	 */
183	function redactedExcerpt(text, index, length) {
184	  const window = 40
185	  const start = Math.max(0, index - window)
186	  const end = Math.min(text.length, index + length + window)
187	  const excerpt = `${start > 0 ? '…' : ''}${text.slice(start, index)}[redacted]${text.slice(index + length, end)}${end < text.length ? '…' : ''}`
188	  return excerpt.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
189	}

199	    hits.push({ record, id: trajectory.id, path, pattern, digest: sha256(match[0]), excerpt: redactedExcerpt(text, match.index, match[0].length) })

228	    totals.outputTokens += step.usage.outputTokens ?? 0
229	    for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens']) {
230	      if (step.usage[key] !== undefined) totals[key] = (totals[key] ?? 0) + step.usage[key]
231	    }
232	  }
233	}
234	
235	/** The model route a stamp names, as `provider/model`. */
236	const routeOf = (model) => `${model.provider}/${model.model}`
237	
238	/**
239	 * Counts one key of one distribution.
240	 * @param {Map<string, Map<string, number>>} distributions every distribution by name
241	 * @param {string} name which distribution
242	 * @param {string} key the bucket
243	 */
244	function tally(distributions, name, key) {
245	  const bucket = distributions.get(name) ?? new Map()
246	  bucket.set(key, (bucket.get(key) ?? 0) + 1)
247	  distributions.set(name, bucket)
248	}
249	
250	/** Sorts a map's entries by key into a plain object, so the manifest reads the same on every build. */
251	function sorted(entries) {
252	  return Object.fromEntries([...entries].sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b)))
253	}
254	
255	/**
256	 * Reads the repository branch and head for the manifest.
257	 * @returns {{ branch: string, head: string }}
258	 */
259	function readRepository() {
260	  const git = (args) => execFileSync('git', ['-C', REPO_DIR, ...args], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim()
261	  return { branch: git(['branch', '--show-current']), head: git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD']) }
262	}
263	
264	/**
265	 * Whether one trajectory's own data-use terms admit the purpose this dataset is
266	 * built for. A record carrying no `terms` states no purpose, so it admits none.
267	 * @param {object} trajectory one parsed trajectory line
268	 * @param {string} purpose the purpose the build names
269	 * @returns {boolean} true when the record's terms list that purpose
270	 */
271	function admitsPurpose(trajectory, purpose) {
272	  return trajectory.terms?.purposes?.includes(purpose) === true
273	}
274	
275	/**
276	 * Reads every record and folds it into the dataset's files and manifest, writing nothing.
277	 * @param {{ name: string, purpose: string | undefined, includeDelegated: boolean, includeHeldOut: boolean }} options what to build
278	 * @returns {{ files: { path: string, content: string }[], manifest: object, hits: object[] }} the built dataset; a non-empty `hits` means it must not be written
279	 */
280	function buildDataset(options) {
281	  const catalog = readTaskCatalog()
282	  const counts = { seen: 0, train: 0, heldout: 0, withheldTerms: 0, withheldHeldOut: 0, delegated: 0, delegatedExcluded: 0, tamperedExcluded: 0, duplicatesDropped: 0 }
283	  const distributions = new Map()
284	  const tokens = newTokenTotals()
285	  const records = []
286	  const hits = []
287	  const seen = new Set()
288	  const trainLines = []
289	  const heldoutLines = []
290	
291	  for (const record of recordNames()) {
292	    const manifestPath = join(RUNS_DIR, record, 'manifest.json')
293	    if (!existsSync(manifestPath)) throw new Error(`${record} holds trajectories.jsonl but no manifest.json`)
294	    const manifestBytes = readFileSync(manifestPath)
295	    const recordManifest = JSON.parse(manifestBytes.toString('utf8'))
296	    records.push({
297	      record,
298	      composition: recordManifest.composition ?? null,
299	      head: recordManifest.repository?.head ?? null,
300	      manifestSha256: sha256(manifestBytes),
301	    })
302	
303	    const lines = readFileSync(join(RUNS_DIR, record, 'trajectories.jsonl'), 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean)
304	    // Sorting by id is stable, so duplicates inside one record stay in export order and the first one wins.
305	    const trajectories = lines.map(line => JSON.parse(line)).sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id))
306	    for (const trajectory of trajectories) {
307	      counts.seen += 1
308	      scanTrajectory(record, trajectory, hits)
309	      if (seen.has(trajectory.id)) { counts.duplicatesDropped += 1; continue }
310	      seen.add(trajectory.id)
311	      // The terms gate runs before every other classification, so a record this
312	      // dataset may not carry reaches no file and no distribution.
313	      if (options.purpose !== undefined && !admitsPurpose(trajectory, options.purpose)) { counts.withheldTerms += 1; continue }
314	      if (trajectory.reward.basis === 'tamper') { counts.tamperedExcluded += 1; continue }
315	
316	      const stamp = trajectory.environment
317	      const task = catalog.get(stamp?.environmentId)
318	      const delegated = (stamp?.implementer ?? 'route') !== 'route'
319	      if (delegated) counts.delegated += 1
320	      const dataset = {
321	        record,
322	        tier: task?.tier ?? null,
323	        domain: task?.domain ?? null,
324	        arm: armOf(stamp?.group),
325	        reward: { value: trajectory.reward.outcome, basis: trajectory.reward.basis },
326	      }
327	      const line = `${JSON.stringify({ ...trajectory, dataset })}\n`
328	
329	      if (stamp?.heldOut === true) {
330	        if (options.includeHeldOut) { heldoutLines.push(line); counts.heldout += 1 }
331	        else counts.withheldHeldOut += 1
332	        continue
333	      }
334	      if (delegated && !options.includeDelegated) { counts.delegatedExcluded += 1; continue }
335	
336	      trainLines.push(line)
337	      counts.train += 1
338	      addUsage(tokens, trajectory.steps)
339	      tally(distributions, 'arm', dataset.arm)
340	      tally(distributions, 'domain', dataset.domain ?? '(none)')
341	      tally(distributions, 'environment', stamp?.environmentId ?? '(none)')
342	      tally(distributions, 'implementer', stamp?.implementer ?? 'route')
343	      tally(distributions, 'ladder', stamp === undefined ? '(none)' : (stamp.ladder ?? [stamp.model]).map(routeOf).join('>'))
344	      tally(distributions, 'model', stamp === undefined ? '(none)' : routeOf(stamp.model))
345	      tally(distributions, 'reward', String(dataset.reward.value))
346	      tally(distributions, 'tier', dataset.tier === null ? '(none)' : String(dataset.tier))
347	    }
348	  }
349	
350	  if (tokens.stepsWithUsage === 0) tokens.note = 'no step of the written set reported usage'
351	  const files = [
352	    { path: 'train.jsonl', content: trainLines.join('') },
353	    { path: 'heldout.jsonl', content: heldoutLines.join('') },
354	  ]
355	  const manifest = {
356	    name: options.name,
357	    format: DATASET_FORMAT,
358	    builtAt: new Date().toISOString(),
359	    repository: readRepository(),
360	    tool: { path: TOOL_PATH, version: TOOL_VERSION },
361	    options: {
362	      purpose: options.purpose ?? null,
363	      includeDelegated: options.includeDelegated,
364	      includeHeldOut: options.includeHeldOut,
365	    },
366	    records,
367	    counts,
368	    distributions: sorted([...distributions].map(([name, bucket]) => [name, sorted(bucket)])),
369	    tokens,
370	    files: files.map(({ path, content }) => ({ path, bytes: Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8'), sha256: sha256(content) })),
371	  }
372	  return { files, manifest, hits }
373	}
374	
375	/**
376	 * One line per count, per distribution, and per written file, for the console.
377	 * @param {object} manifest the manifest {@link buildDataset} produced
378	 * @returns {string} the summary, newline-joined
379	 */
380	function formatSummary(manifest) {
381	  const { counts, tokens } = manifest
382	  const purpose = manifest.options.purpose
383	  const lines = [
384	    `${manifest.name}: ${counts.train} train, ${counts.heldout} held out, of ${counts.seen} trajectories in ${manifest.records.length} records${purpose === null ? '' : ` admitted for ${purpose}`}`,
385	    `  excluded: ${counts.withheldTerms} withheld by terms, ${counts.withheldHeldOut} withheld held-out, ${counts.delegatedExcluded} delegated (${counts.delegated} seen), ${counts.tamperedExcluded} tampered, ${counts.duplicatesDropped} duplicates`,
386	    `  tokens: ${tokens.inputTokens} input, ${tokens.outputTokens} output, ${tokens.cacheReadTokens ?? 0} cache-read, ${tokens.cacheWriteTokens ?? 0} cache-write over ${tokens.stepsWithUsage} of ${tokens.steps} steps${tokens.note === undefined ? '' : ` (${tokens.note})`}`,
387	  ]
388	  for (const [name, bucket] of Object.entries(manifest.distributions)) {
389	    lines.push(`  ${name}: ${Object.entries(bucket).map(([key, count]) => `${key}=${count}`).join(' ')}`)
390	  }
391	  for (const file of manifest.files) lines.push(`  ${file.path}: ${file.bytes} bytes, ${file.sha256}`)
392	  return lines.join('\n')
393	}
394	
395	/**
396	 * Compares a rebuilt dataset with the manifest recorded beside it, and with
397	 * whichever of its files the repository carries.
398	 * @param {string} directory the dataset directory
399	 * @param {{ manifest: object }} built what {@link buildDataset} produced
400	 * @returns {string[]} one line per drift, empty when the recorded manifest matches
401	 */
402	function checkDataset(directory, built) {
403	  const manifestPath = join(directory, 'manifest.json')
404	  if (!existsSync(manifestPath)) return [`${relative(REPO_DIR, manifestPath)} does not exist; build the dataset first`]
405	  const recorded = JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifestPath, 'utf8'))
406	  const drift = []
407	  for (const file of built.manifest.files) {
408	    const entry = recorded.files.find(candidate => candidate.path === file.path)
409	    if (entry === undefined) { drift.push(`${file.path}: the recorded manifest lists no such file`); continue }
410	    if (entry.sha256 !== file.sha256) drift.push(`${file.path}: rebuilt ${file.sha256}, manifest records ${entry.sha256}`)
411	    if (entry.bytes !== file.bytes) drift.push(`${file.path}: rebuilt ${file.bytes} bytes, manifest records ${entry.bytes}`)
412	    const onDisk = join(directory, file.path)
413	    // A dataset too large to commit keeps only its manifest, so an absent file is not drift.
414	    if (existsSync(onDisk) && sha256(readFileSync(onDisk)) !== entry.sha256) drift.push(`${file.path}: the file in the repository does not match the manifest`)
415	  }
416	  for (const entry of recorded.files) {
417	    if (!built.manifest.files.some(file => file.path === entry.path)) drift.push(`${entry.path}: the rebuild writes no such file`)
418	  }
419	  if (JSON.stringify(recorded.counts) !== JSON.stringify(built.manifest.counts)) drift.push('counts: the rebuild does not reproduce the recorded counts')
420	  return drift
421	}
422	
423	function main() {
424	  const options = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2))
425	  const directory = join(DATASETS_DIR, options.name)
426	  const built = buildDataset(options)
427	
428	  if (built.hits.length > 0) {
429	    console.error(`refusing to build ${relative(REPO_DIR, directory)}: ${built.hits.length} credential- or mailbox-shaped match(es); re-export the record, there is no accept flag`)
430	    for (const hit of built.hits) console.error(`  ${hit.record} ${hit.id} ${hit.path} ${hit.pattern} sha256=${hit.digest} ${hit.excerpt}`)
431	    process.exit(1)
432	  }
433	
434	  if (options.check) {
435	    const drift = checkDataset(directory, built)
436	    if (drift.length > 0) {
437	      console.error(`${relative(REPO_DIR, directory)} has drifted from its manifest:`)
438	      for (const line of drift) console.error(`  ${line}`)
439	      process.exit(1)
440	    }
441	    console.log(`${relative(REPO_DIR, directory)}: the rebuild matches the recorded manifest`)
442	    return
443	  }
444	
445	  mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true })
446	  for (const file of built.files) writeFileSync(join(directory, file.path), file.content)
447	  writeFileSync(join(directory, 'manifest.json'), `${JSON.stringify(built.manifest, null, 2)}\n`)
448	  console.log(`wrote ${relative(REPO_DIR, directory)}`)
449	  console.log(formatSummary(built.manifest))
450	}
451	
452	main()

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	// Records one Proving Ground run under data/proving-ground/<name>/: copies the
3	// driver's exports and every cell and shift session log out of the directory
4	// the driver ran in, and writes a manifest with the repository head, the
5	// composition, the implementer, the session ids, and every file's SHA-256.
6	// Node built-ins only.
7	//
8	// Usage: node record-run.mjs <run-directory> <name> --composition <path> [--elapsed-seconds <n>] [--partial <reason>]
9	//
10	//   <run-directory>   where the driver ran: holds facts.jsonl, trajectories.jsonl,
11	//                     observatory.json, observatory.html, .sessions/, and either
12	//                     stdout.jsonl (a fleet driver's result line) or status.json
13	//                     (a shift driver's status)
14	//   <name>            the run directory name, e.g. 2026-09-06-claude-code-run-2
15	//   --composition     repository-relative cordis.yml the driver booted
16	//   --elapsed-seconds wall time of the run when the driver did not record it
17	//   --partial         record a run whose driver died before writing its result:
18	//                     the session logs are kept, result.json states only
19	//                     `{ type: 'partial', reason }`, and the manifest carries the
20	//                     reason, so the cells that ran stay evidence without a
21	//                     verdict the driver never computed
22	//
23	// The run directory is written once; an existing target is refused so a
24	// recorded run is never rewritten in place. Recording prints the escape census
25	// of the new record (`census-escapes.mjs`), so what each cell reached outside
26	// its own workspace is read at the moment the run enters the corpus.
27	
28	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
29	import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
30	import { join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
31	import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
32	import { censusRecord, formatCensus } from './census-escapes.mjs'
33	import { formatTotals, summarizeRun } from './summarize-run.mjs'
34	
35	const REPO_DIR = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..', '..', '..')
36	const RUNS_DIR = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..')
37	const EXPORTS = ['facts.jsonl', 'trajectories.jsonl', 'observatory.json', 'observatory.html']
38	
39	/**
40	 * Parses the command line.
41	 * @param {string[]} argv arguments after the script path
42	 * @returns {{ runDirectory: string, name: string, composition: string, elapsedSeconds: number | undefined, partial: string | undefined }}
43	 */
44	function parseArgs(argv) {
45	  const positional = []
46	  const options = { composition: undefined, elapsedSeconds: undefined, partial: undefined }
47	  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
48	    const arg = argv[i]
49	    if (arg === '--composition') { options.composition = argv[++i] }
50	    else if (arg === '--elapsed-seconds') { options.elapsedSeconds = Number(argv[++i]) }
51	    else if (arg === '--partial') { options.partial = argv[++i] }
52	    else positional.push(arg)
53	  }
54	  const [runDirectory, name] = positional
55	  if (runDirectory === undefined || name === undefined || options.composition === undefined || options.partial === '') {
56	    throw new Error('usage: node record-run.mjs <run-directory> <name> --composition <path> [--elapsed-seconds <n>] [--partial <reason>]')
57	  }
58	  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/.test(name)) throw new Error(`run name must be a plain directory name: ${name}`)
59	  return { runDirectory: resolve(runDirectory), name, ...options }
60	}
61	
62	/**
63	 * @param {Buffer | string} content bytes to digest
64	 * @returns {string} lowercase hex SHA-256
65	 */
66	function sha256(content) {
67	  return createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
68	}
69	
70	/**
71	 * Finds every session log the driver's persistence root holds.
72	 * @param {string} runDirectory where the driver ran
73	 * @returns {{ sessionId: string, path: string }[]}
74	 */
75	function sessionLogs(runDirectory) {
76	  const root = join(runDirectory, '.sessions')
77	  if (!existsSync(root)) return []
78	  const logs = []
79	  const walk = (directory) => {
80	    for (const name of readdirSync(directory)) {
81	      const path = join(directory, name)
82	      if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) walk(path)
83	      else if (name === 'session.jsonl') logs.push({ sessionId: relative(root, directory).split('/').at(-1), path })
84	    }
85	  }
86	  walk(root)
87	  return logs.sort((a, b) => a.sessionId.localeCompare(b.sessionId))
88	}
89	
90	/**
91	 * Reads the driver's result: a fleet driver's last stdout line or a shift driver's status file.
92	 * A run recorded with `--partial` has neither, and its result states only the reason.
93	 * @param {string} runDirectory where the driver ran
94	 * @param {string | undefined} partial why the driver wrote no result, when the run is recorded without one
95	 * @returns {{ kind: 'result' | 'status' | 'partial', value: Record<string, unknown> }}
96	 */
97	function driverResult(runDirectory, partial) {
98	  const stdout = join(runDirectory, 'stdout.jsonl')
99	  if (existsSync(stdout)) {
100	    const lines = readFileSync(stdout, 'utf8').trim().split('\n')
101	    const last = JSON.parse(lines.at(-1))
102	    if (last.type === 'result') return { kind: 'result', value: last }
103	  }
104	  const status = join(runDirectory, 'status.json')
105	  if (existsSync(status)) return { kind: 'status', value: JSON.parse(readFileSync(status, 'utf8')) }
106	  if (partial !== undefined) return { kind: 'partial', value: { type: 'partial', reason: partial } }
107	  throw new Error(`${runDirectory} holds neither a result line in stdout.jsonl nor a status.json; pass --partial <reason> to record the cells that ran without one`)
108	}
109	
110	/**
111	 * Folds the run stamps out of the session logs: environment ids per session, the implementer, the district, and the isolation.
112	 * @param {{ sessionId: string, path: string }[]} logs every session log of the run
113	 * @returns {{ sessions: Record<string, string>, implementers: string[], districts: string[], isolations: string[], startedAt: number | undefined, endedAt: number | undefined }}
114	 */
115	function foldStamps(logs) {
116	  const sessions = {}
117	  const implementers = new Set()
118	  const districts = new Set()
119	  const isolations = new Set()
120	  let startedAt
121	  let endedAt
122	  for (const { sessionId, path } of logs) {
123	    for (const line of readFileSync(path, 'utf8').trim().split('\n')) {
124	      const event = JSON.parse(line)
125	      // The header line carries `createdAt`; every event line carries `time`.
126	      const at = typeof event.time === 'number' ? event.time : event.createdAt
127	      if (typeof at === 'number') {
128	        startedAt = startedAt === undefined ? at : Math.min(startedAt, at)
129	        endedAt = endedAt === undefined ? at : Math.max(endedAt, at)
130	      }
131	      if (event.type !== 'environment/run') continue
132	      sessions[event.data.environmentId] = sessionId
133	      if (event.data.implementer !== undefined) implementers.add(event.data.implementer)
134	      if (event.data.district !== undefined) districts.add(event.data.district)
135	      if (event.data.isolation !== undefined) isolations.add(event.data.isolation)
136	    }
137	  }
138	  return { sessions, implementers: [...implementers].sort(), districts: [...districts].sort(), isolations: [...isolations].sort(), startedAt, endedAt }
139	}
140	
141	function main() {
142	  const { runDirectory, name, composition, elapsedSeconds, partial } = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2))
143	  const target = join(RUNS_DIR, name)
144	  if (existsSync(target)) throw new Error(`${relative(REPO_DIR, target)} already exists; a recorded run is never rewritten`)
145	  if (!existsSync(join(REPO_DIR, composition))) throw new Error(`composition ${composition} is not in the repository`)
146	
147	  const result = driverResult(runDirectory, partial)
148	  const logs = sessionLogs(runDirectory)
149	  const stamps = foldStamps(logs)
150	  mkdirSync(join(target, 'sessions'), { recursive: true })
151	
152	  const files = []
153	  const record = (relativePath, content) => {
154	    const path = join(target, relativePath)
155	    writeFileSync(path, content)
156	    files.push({ path: relativePath, bytes: content.length, sha256: sha256(content) })
157	  }
158	  record('result.json', Buffer.from(`${JSON.stringify(result.value, null, 2)}\n`))
159	  for (const exportName of EXPORTS) {
160	    const source = join(runDirectory, exportName)
161	    if (existsSync(source)) record(exportName, readFileSync(source))
162	  }
163	  for (const { sessionId, path } of logs) record(`sessions/${sessionId}.jsonl`, readFileSync(path))
164	
165	  const git = (args) => execFileSync('git', ['-C', REPO_DIR, ...args], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim()
166	  const manifest = {
167	    run: name,
168	    ranAt: stamps.startedAt === undefined ? undefined : new Date(stamps.startedAt).toISOString(),
169	    endedAt: stamps.endedAt === undefined ? undefined : new Date(stamps.endedAt).toISOString(),
170	    elapsedSeconds: elapsedSeconds ?? (stamps.startedAt === undefined || stamps.endedAt === undefined ? undefined : Math.round((stamps.endedAt - stamps.startedAt) / 1000)),
171	    repository: { branch: git(['branch', '--show-current']), head: git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD']) },
172	    composition,
173	    driverResult: result.kind,
174	    ...partial === undefined ? {} : { partial },
175	    districts: stamps.districts,
176	    implementers: stamps.implementers,
177	    isolations: stamps.isolations,
178	    sessions: stamps.sessions,
179	    files,
180	  }
181	  writeFileSync(join(target, 'manifest.json'), `${JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2)}\n`)
182	  console.log(`recorded ${relative(REPO_DIR, target)}: ${files.length} files, ${logs.length} session logs, implementers ${stamps.implementers.join(', ') || 'none'}`)
183	  // The census and the totals read the run as recorded, so what they print is
184	  // what any later reader of this directory gets from `census-escapes.mjs`
185	  // and `summarize-run.mjs`.
186	  console.log(formatCensus(censusRecord(target)))
187	  console.log(formatTotals(summarizeRun(target)))
188	}
189	
190	main()
