1	/**
2	 * Pure projection of one session log into a {@link Trajectory}: surface
3	 * messages with their source seqs, per-step usage, the reward the log's goal
4	 * and verification events decide, the weighted pass rate of the last recorded
5	 * run beside it, the data-use terms the log pins, and the components in play.
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories
7	 */
8	
9	import { ComponentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
10	import type { ComponentId as ComponentIdType } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
11	import { termsOf } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use'
12	import { decodeEnvironmentRun } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
13	import type { EnvironmentRunStamp } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
14	import { decodeGoalChange } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
15	import type { GoalSnapshot } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal/types'
16	import type { ContentBlock, ToolCallBlock } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
17	import { foldSurface } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
18	import type { EpochHeader, SessionEvent, SessionHeader } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
19	import { foldVerification } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
20	import type {
21	  Trajectory,
22	  TrajectoryMessage,
23	  TrajectoryReward,
24	  TrajectoryStep,
25	  TrajectoryTerms,
26	  TrajectoryToolCall,
27	} from './types.ts'
28	
29	/** The record format tag every exported line carries. */
30	export const TRAJECTORY_FORMAT = 'dsh-trajectory/2'
31	
32	/** Position of a surface event inside the turn/step structure. */
33	interface StepPosition {
34	  readonly turn: number
35	  readonly step: number
36	}
37	
38	/** Everything one sequential pass over the log collects before the surface is projected. */
39	interface LogScan {
40	  header?: EpochHeader
41	  agentPreset?: string
42	  environment?: EnvironmentRunStamp
43	  readonly positions: Map<number, StepPosition>
44	  readonly steps: TrajectoryStep[]
45	  readonly toolNames: string[]
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * Read the preset selection from a log-only event this package does not
50	 * declare. The event belongs to `dsh-agent-presets`; reading it by name keeps
51	 * the fold free of that dependency, and the payload check is the durable-log
52	 * boundary's own validation.
53	 */
54	function presetOf(event: SessionEvent): string | undefined {
55	  if ((event.type as string) !== 'agent-preset/selected') return undefined
56	  const data = event.data as { agentPreset?: unknown }
57	  return typeof data.agentPreset === 'string' ? data.agentPreset : undefined
58	}
59	
60	/** One ordered pass over every event, collecting what the projection needs. */
61	function scanLog(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): LogScan {
62	  const scan: LogScan = {
63	    positions: new Map(),
64	    steps: [],
65	    toolNames: [],
66	  }
67	  let position: StepPosition | undefined
68	  for (const event of events) {
69	    switch (event.type) {
70	      case 'request/header':
71	        scan.header = event.data.header
72	        break
73	      case 'step/start':
74	        position = { turn: event.data.turn, step: event.data.step }
75	        scan.steps.push(position)
76	        break
77	      case 'step/end':
78	        position = undefined
79	        break
80	      case 'user/message':
81	      case 'tool/result':
82	        if (position !== undefined) scan.positions.set(event.seq, position)
83	        break
84	      case 'assistant/message': {
85	        if (position !== undefined) scan.positions.set(event.seq, position)
86	        const usage = event.data.usage
87	        if (usage !== undefined) {
88	          const index = scan.steps.findIndex(step => step.turn === event.data.turn && step.step === event.data.step)
89	          if (index !== -1) scan.steps[index] = { ...scan.steps[index] as TrajectoryStep, usage }
90	        }
91	        break
92	      }
93	      case 'tool/call':
94	        if (!scan.toolNames.includes(event.data.name)) scan.toolNames.push(event.data.name)
95	        break
96	      case 'environment/run': {
97	        // The durable boundary validates the stamp; a malformed one fails the fold loudly.
98	        const stamp = decodeEnvironmentRun(event.data)
99	        if (stamp !== undefined) scan.environment = stamp
100	        break
101	      }
102	      default: {
103	        const preset = presetOf(event)
104	        if (preset !== undefined) scan.agentPreset = preset
105	      }
106	    }
107	  }
108	  return scan
109	}
110	
111	/** Tool calls an assistant message requested, from its own blocks. */
112	function toolCallsOf(content: readonly ContentBlock[]): TrajectoryToolCall[] {
113	  return content
114	    .filter((block): block is ToolCallBlock => block.type === 'tool-call')
115	    .map(block => ({ id: block.id, name: block.name, arguments: block.arguments }))
116	}
117	
118	/** Project one surface event to a trajectory message, or nothing for an empty assistant step. */
119	function projectMessage(event: SessionEvent, position: StepPosition | undefined): TrajectoryMessage | undefined {
120	  const at = position === undefined ? {} : { turn: position.turn, step: position.step }
121	  switch (event.type) {
122	    case 'user/message':
123	      return { role: 'user', seq: event.seq, ...at, content: event.data.content, sourceKind: event.data.source.kind }
124	    case 'assistant/message': {
125	      const message = event.data.message
126	      if (message.content.length === 0) return undefined
127	      const toolCalls = toolCallsOf(message.content)
128	      return {
129	        role: 'assistant',
130	        seq: event.seq,
131	        ...at,
132	        content: message.content,
133	        sourceKind: message.source.kind,
134	        ...toolCalls.length === 0 ? {} : { toolCalls },
135	      }
136	    }
137	    case 'tool/result': {
138	      const [block] = event.data.message.content
139	      return {
140	        role: 'tool',
141	        seq: event.seq,
142	        ...at,
143	        content: block.content,
144	        sourceKind: event.data.message.source.kind,
145	        toolCallId: block.toolCallId,
146	        ...block.isError === true ? { isError: true } : {},
147	      }
148	    }
149	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- the surface fold admits only the three message-producing types. */
150	    default:
151	      return undefined
152	  }
153	}
154	
155	/** The goal the reward measures, as the last non-clear mutation left it. */
156	interface RewardGoal {
157	  goal?: GoalSnapshot
158	  completed: boolean
159	}
160	
161	/** Fold the current goal and whether the log completed it. */
162	function scanGoal(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): RewardGoal {
163	  const scanned: RewardGoal = { completed: false }
164	  for (const event of events) {
165	    if (event.type !== 'goal/change') continue
166	    const change = decodeGoalChange(event.data)
167	    if (change === undefined || change.operation === 'clear') continue
168	    scanned.goal = change.goal
169	    scanned.completed = change.operation === 'complete'
170	  }
171	  return scanned
172	}
173	
174	/**
175	 * Decide one session's reward from its goal and verification events alone: a
176	 * tampered last run outranks everything, the verifier decides whenever a
177	 * standard exists, an uncertified completion is undecided, and a log without a
178	 * goal is unmeasured.
179	 * @param events - the session's contiguous event log.
180	 * @returns the reward outcome with its basis, the measured goal, the covering certificate, and the counts behind them.
181	 */
182	export function foldTrajectoryReward(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TrajectoryReward {
183	  const verification = foldVerification(events)
184	  const scanned = scanGoal(events)
185	  const goal = scanned.goal === undefined
186	    ? {}
187	    : { goal: { id: scanned.goal.id, objective: scanned.goal.objective, phase: scanned.goal.phase } }
188	  const counts = {
189	    directives: verification.directivesIssued,
190	    relaxations: verification.standard?.relaxed.length ?? 0,
191	    attempts: verification.runsRecorded,
192	  }
193	  // A tampered run means the checks stopped describing the task, so no
194	  // certificate and no goal phase in the same log can earn credit for it.
195	  if (verification.lastRun?.verdict === 'tampered') return { outcome: 0, basis: 'tamper', ...goal, ...counts }
196	  if (verification.standard !== undefined) {
197	    return verification.certificate === undefined
198	      ? { outcome: 0, basis: 'certificate', ...goal, ...counts }
199	      : { outcome: 1, basis: 'certificate', ...goal, certificate: verification.certificate, ...counts }
200	  }
201	  if (scanned.completed) return { outcome: null, basis: 'uncertified-completion', ...goal, ...counts }
202	  return { outcome: null, basis: 'none', ...goal, ...counts }
203	}
204	
205	/**
206	 * The admission-relevant part of the session's pinned terms, read through the
207	 * {@link termsOf} fold `@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use` owns so the record states
208	 * exactly the terms a curated export gates on.
209	 * @param events - the session's contiguous event log.
210	 * @returns the agreement and the purposes it admits, or `undefined` for a log carrying no `dataUse/terms`.
211	 */
212	function termsFrom(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TrajectoryTerms | undefined {
213	  const terms = termsOf(events)
214	  return terms === undefined ? undefined : { agreementId: terms.agreementId, purposes: [...terms.purposes] }
215	}
216	
217	/** Component ids in play, in the component registry's id scheme. */
218	function componentsOf(scan: LogScan): ComponentIdType[] {
219	  const ids: string[] = []
220	  if (scan.agentPreset !== undefined) ids.push(`composition:${scan.agentPreset}`)
221	  if (scan.environment !== undefined) ids.push(`environment:${scan.environment.environmentId}`)
222	  if (scan.header !== undefined) ids.push(`model-provider:${scan.header.config.provider}`)
223	  for (const name of scan.toolNames) ids.push(`tool:${name}`)
224	  return ids.map(ComponentId)
225	}
226	
227	/**
228	 * Fold one session into its trajectory.
229	 * @param meta - the session header.
230	 * @param events - the session's contiguous event log.
231	 * @returns the trajectory; deterministic for the same inputs.
232	 */
233	export function foldTrajectory(meta: SessionHeader, events: readonly SessionEvent[]): Trajectory {
234	  const scan = scanLog(events)
235	  const bySeq = new Map(events.map(event => [event.seq, event] as const))
236	  const messages: TrajectoryMessage[] = []
237	  for (const seq of foldSurface(events).nodes) {
238	    const event = bySeq.get(seq)
239	    /* v8 ignore next -- surface nodes cite seqs of the log they were folded from. */
240	    if (event === undefined) continue
241	    const message = projectMessage(event, scan.positions.get(seq))
242	    if (message !== undefined) messages.push(message)
243	  }
244	  const reward = foldTrajectoryReward(events)
245	  const parity = foldVerification(events).lastRun?.parity
246	  const header = scan.header
247	  const terms = termsFrom(events)
248	  return {
249	    format: TRAJECTORY_FORMAT,
250	    id: meta.id,
251	    source: {
252	      sessionId: meta.id,
253	      createdAt: meta.createdAt,
254	      ...meta.cwd === undefined ? {} : { cwd: meta.cwd },
255	      ...meta.parentSession === undefined ? {} : { parentSession: meta.parentSession },
256	      ...scan.agentPreset === undefined ? {} : { agentPreset: scan.agentPreset },
257	    },
258	    ...terms === undefined ? {} : { terms },
259	    ...scan.environment === undefined ? {} : { environment: scan.environment },
260	    ...header === undefined ? {} : { config: header.config },
261	    ...header?.system === undefined ? {} : { system: header.system },
262	    ...header?.tools === undefined ? {} : { tools: header.tools },
263	    messages,
264	    steps: scan.steps,
265	    reward,
266	    ...parity === undefined ? {} : { parity },
267	    provenance: {
268	      components: componentsOf(scan),
269	      toolNames: scan.toolNames,
270	      ...reward.certificate === undefined ? {} : { isolation: reward.certificate.isolation },
271	    },
272	  }
273	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the trajectory record: the `dsh-trajectory/2` line format a
3	 * trainer or a leaderboard reads, free of host-side imports.
4	 *
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories/types
6	 */
7	
8	import type { ComponentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
9	import type { DataUsePurpose } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use'
10	import type { EnvironmentRunStamp } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
11	import type { GoalId, GoalPhase } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal/types'
12	import type { CallId, ContentBlock, LlmCallConfig, TokenUsage, ToolSchema } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
13	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types'
14	import type { CertificateIsolation, RunParity, VerificationCertificate } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
15	
16	/** The record format tag every exported line carries. */
17	export type TrajectoryFormat = 'dsh-trajectory/2'
18	
19	/**
20	 * The data-use terms the session was held under, as the admission rule reads
21	 * them: a consumer building a corpus for one purpose keeps the record only when
22	 * {@link TrajectoryTerms.purposes} lists it. Retention, residency, and the
23	 * client are not carried, because no admission decision reads them.
24	 */
25	export interface TrajectoryTerms {
26	  /** The agreement the session's terms come from. */
27	  readonly agreementId: string
28	  /** Purposes the terms admit; a purpose absent from this list is refused. */
29	  readonly purposes: readonly DataUsePurpose[]
30	}
31	
32	/** Where the trajectory came from: the session and the composition that ran it. */
33	export interface TrajectorySource {
34	  /** Session the trajectory was folded from. */
35	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
36	  /** Session creation time, epoch milliseconds. */
37	  readonly createdAt: number
38	  /** Working directory the session ran in, when the header recorded one. */
39	  readonly cwd?: string
40	  /** Session this one was forked from, when the header recorded one. */
41	  readonly parentSession?: SessionId
42	  /** Agent preset the session last selected, when the log recorded one. */
43	  readonly agentPreset?: string
44	}
45	
46	/** Roles of the exported chat message list. */
47	export type TrajectoryMessageRole = 'user' | 'assistant' | 'tool'
48	
49	/** One tool invocation an assistant message requested. */
50	export interface TrajectoryToolCall {
51	  /** Provider-issued call id, matched by the tool message's `toolCallId`. */
52	  readonly id: CallId
53	  /** Registered tool name. */
54	  readonly name: string
55	  /** Raw JSON argument string exactly as the model produced it. */
56	  readonly arguments: string
57	}
58	
59	/** One model-visible message of the trajectory, projected from a surface event. */
60	export interface TrajectoryMessage {
61	  /** Chat role. */
62	  readonly role: TrajectoryMessageRole
63	  /** Seq of the session event this message came from. */
64	  readonly seq: number
65	  /** Turn the message belongs to, absent when it precedes the first turn. */
66	  readonly turn?: number
67	  /** Step the message belongs to, absent outside a step. */
68	  readonly step?: number
69	  /** Exact model-facing content blocks; reasoning blocks are kept. */
70	  readonly content: readonly ContentBlock[]
71	  /** Message source kind as the session recorded it (`user`, `plugin`, `model`, `tool`, or a plugin's own kind). */
72	  readonly sourceKind: string
73	  /** Tool calls the assistant requested, present only on assistant messages that requested any. */
74	  readonly toolCalls?: readonly TrajectoryToolCall[]
75	  /** Call this tool message answers, present only on tool messages. */
76	  readonly toolCallId?: CallId
77	  /** Whether the tool reported an error, present only on tool messages that did. */
78	  readonly isError?: true
79	}
80	
81	/** One model call of the trajectory with its token accounting. */
82	export interface TrajectoryStep {
83	  readonly turn: number
84	  readonly step: number
85	  /** Token usage the adapter reported for this step, absent when it reported none. */
86	  readonly usage?: TokenUsage
87	}
88	
89	/**
90	 * How the reward was decided: `tamper` when the last recorded run found the
91	 * check-owned files changed, which voids the measurement whatever else the log
92	 * says; `certificate` when a completion standard existed for the goal (the
93	 * verifier decided); `uncertified-completion` when the goal completed with no
94	 * standard ever authored; `none` when the log holds no goal.
95	 */
96	export type TrajectoryRewardBasis = 'tamper' | 'certificate' | 'uncertified-completion' | 'none'
97	
98	/** The goal the reward measures, as the log last recorded it. */
99	export interface TrajectoryGoal {
100	  readonly id: GoalId
101	  readonly objective: string
102	  readonly phase: GoalPhase
103	}
104	
105	/** The reward with its basis and the evidence behind it. */
106	export interface TrajectoryReward {
107	  /** `1` for a certified completion, `0` for a measured goal without a covering certificate, `null` when no verifier decided. */
108	  readonly outcome: 1 | 0 | null
109	  readonly basis: TrajectoryRewardBasis
110	  /** Goal the reward measures, absent when the log holds none. */
111	  readonly goal?: TrajectoryGoal
112	  /** Certificate covering the current standard revision, present only when `outcome` is `1`. */
113	  readonly certificate?: VerificationCertificate
114	  /** Directives the validator issued during the session. */
115	  readonly directives: number
116	  /** Checks relaxed out of the standard during the session. */
117	  readonly relaxations: number
118	  /** Runs of the standard recorded during the session, passing or failing. */
119	  readonly attempts: number
120	}
121	
122	/** What was in play while the trajectory ran, in the component registry's id scheme. */
123	export interface TrajectoryProvenance {
124	  /** Component ids: the preset composition, the model provider, and every tool called, in first-use order. */
125	  readonly components: readonly ComponentId[]
126	  /** Tool names called, in first-use order. */
127	  readonly toolNames: readonly string[]
128	  /** Isolation level of the covering certificate, absent without one. */
129	  readonly isolation?: CertificateIsolation
130	}
131	
132	/** One exported trajectory: a session as a trainer reads it. */
133	export interface Trajectory {
134	  readonly format: TrajectoryFormat
135	  /** Trajectory identity, the session id. */
136	  readonly id: SessionId
137	  readonly source: TrajectorySource
138	  /**
139	   * The newest `dataUse/terms` the session log carries. Absent for a session
140	   * whose log carries none, and absence admits no purpose at all: a consumer
141	   * filtering by purpose withholds such a record rather than assuming one.
142	   */
143	  readonly terms?: TrajectoryTerms
144	  /** The environment the session ran, from its `environment/run` stamp; absent for a session no runner stamped. */
145	  readonly environment?: EnvironmentRunStamp
146	  /** Call configuration of the last logged request header, absent for a session that made no request. */
147	  readonly config?: LlmCallConfig
148	  /** Rendered system prompt of the last logged request header, absent for a system-less request. */
149	  readonly system?: string
150	  /** Tool schemas of the last logged request header, absent for a tool-less request. */
151	  readonly tools?: readonly ToolSchema[]
152	  /** Model-visible messages in surface order. */
153	  readonly messages: readonly TrajectoryMessage[]
154	  /** Model calls in log order. */
155	  readonly steps: readonly TrajectoryStep[]
156	  readonly reward: TrajectoryReward
157	  /**
158	   * Weighted pass rate of the last recorded run, absent when that run measured
159	   * no cases. It is an auxiliary signal a training run may shape with and never
160	   * a replacement for the certificate-based {@link TrajectoryReward.outcome}: a
161	   * pass rate is gameable by a candidate that overfits the failures it was
162	   * shown and abandons the rest.
163	   */
164	  readonly parity?: RunParity
165	  readonly provenance: TrajectoryProvenance
166	}
167	
168	/** Destination of exported lines; the exporter closes it when the export settles. */
169	export interface TrajectorySink {
170	  /**
171	   * Accept one complete line, newline included.
172	   * @param line - one serialized trajectory followed by `\n`.
173	   */
174	  write(line: string): Promise<void> | void
175	  /** Release the destination; called exactly once, after the last write or after a failure. */
176	  close(): Promise<void> | void
177	}
178	
179	/** What to export and where. */
180	export interface TrajectoryExportRequest {
181	  /** Sessions to export; absent exports every persisted session. */
182	  readonly sessions?: readonly SessionId[]
183	  /** Destination of the lines. */
184	  readonly sink: TrajectorySink
185	  /** Write only trajectories whose reward outcome is `1`. */
186	  readonly rewardedOnly?: boolean
187	  /** Also write sessions whose environment is held out; absent withholds them, so evaluation tasks never train by default. */
188	  readonly includeHeldOut?: boolean
189	  /**
190	   * Districts to export: a session is written only when its stamp carries one
191	   * of these, so a named list reaches a district the deployment otherwise
192	   * withholds. Absent applies the configured `withheldDistricts` instead.
193	   */
194	  readonly districts?: readonly string[]
195	}
196	
197	/** One session the export could not read. */
198	export interface TrajectoryExportSkip {
199	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
200	  /** The read or fold failure, as a message. */
201	  readonly reason: string
202	}
203	
204	/** Counts of one export. */
205	export interface TrajectoryExportReport {
206	  /** Sessions the request named or the store listed. */
207	  readonly sessions: number
208	  /** Lines written. */
209	  readonly exported: number
210	  /** Written lines whose reward outcome is `1`. */
211	  readonly rewarded: number
212	  /** Readable sessions withheld by `rewardedOnly`. */
213	  readonly filtered: number
214	  /** Readable sessions withheld because their environment is held out. */
215	  readonly heldOut: number
216	  /** Readable sessions withheld because their stamp's district is not one this export writes. */
217	  readonly withheld: number
218	  /** Sessions that could not be read or folded. */
219	  readonly skipped: readonly TrajectoryExportSkip[]
220	}

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

</system-reminder>

1	/**
2	 * Curated export: the trajectory exporter wrapped in the two rules a transcript
3	 * may not leave the lab without. It refuses to run without a redaction profile,
4	 * withholds every session whose pinned `dataUse/terms` do not admit the
5	 * export's purpose, redacts the record before it reaches the sink, and writes
6	 * one {@link ExportManifest} beside the lines. It reads persisted logs and
7	 * writes no session event. The
8	 * [curator Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-curator.md)
9	 * owns the design rationale.
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-curator
11	 */
12	
13	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
14	import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
15	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
16	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
17	// The value import also resolves ctx.dataUse.
18	import { termsOf } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use'
19	import type { DataUseTerms } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use'
20	// Type-only: resolves ctx.sessionPersistence.
21	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
22	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types'
23	// The value import also resolves ctx.trajectories.
24	import { TRAJECTORY_FORMAT } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'
25	import type { Trajectory, TrajectoryExportSkip } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories/types'
26	import { compileProfile, CuratorError, redactTrajectory } from './redaction.ts'
27	import type { RedactionProfile } from './redaction.ts'
28	import type {
29	  CuratedExportReport,
30	  CuratedExportRequest,
31	  CuratedTrajectory,
32	  ExportManifest,
33	  RedactionProfileConfig,
34	} from './types.ts'
35	
36	export type * from './types.ts'
37	export {
38	  applyRules,
39	  CuratorError,
40	  redactTrajectory,
41	  SHIPPED_REDACTION_RULES,
42	  compileProfile,
43	  type CompiledRedactionRule,
44	  type CuratorErrorCode,
45	  type RedactionProfile,
46	} from './redaction.ts'
47	
48	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
49	  interface Context {
50	    curator: CuratorService
51	  }
52	}
53	
54	/** Format tag every {@link ExportManifest} carries. */
55	export const EXPORT_MANIFEST_VERSION = 'dsh-export-manifest/1'
56	
57	/** Deployment choices of the curated export, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
58	export interface Config {
59	  /**
60	   * Redaction profiles by id, at least one. Redaction is not optional: there is
61	   * no configuration under which a curated export runs without a profile, so a
62	   * deployment states here which profiles it can export under.
63	   */
64	  profiles: Record<string, RedactionProfileConfig>
65	  /** Profile an export that names none applies; an export with neither is refused. */
66	  defaultProfile?: string
67	}
68	
69	/** Curated export (`ctx.curator`): redacted, terms-gated trajectory export with a manifest. */
70	export class CuratorService extends Service {
71	  static inject = ['trajectories', 'sessionPersistence', 'dataUse']
72	
73	  // Inline schema call: the config catalog walks `static Config` statically.
74	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
75	    profiles: z.dict(z.object({
76	      shipped: z.boolean().required(),
77	      rules: z.array(z.object({
78	        id: z.string().required(),
79	        pattern: z.string().required(),
80	        flags: z.string(),
81	        replacement: z.string().required(),
82	      })).default([]),
83	    })).required(),
84	    defaultProfile: z.string(),
85	  })
86	
87	  private readonly profiles: Map<string, RedactionProfile>
88	  private readonly defaultProfile: string | undefined
89	
90	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
91	    super(ctx, 'curator')
92	    const entries = Object.entries(config.profiles)
93	    if (entries.length === 0) {
94	      throw new CuratorError('profiles is empty, so this deployment could export under no profile at all', 'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG')
95	    }
96	    this.profiles = new Map(entries.map(([id, profile]) => [id, compileProfile(id, profile)]))
97	    if (config.defaultProfile !== undefined && !this.profiles.has(config.defaultProfile)) {
98	      throw new CuratorError(
99	        `defaultProfile "${config.defaultProfile}" is not one of the configured profiles ${[...this.profiles.keys()].join(', ')}`,
100	        'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG',
101	      )
102	    }
103	    this.defaultProfile = config.defaultProfile
104	  }
105	
106	  /**
107	   * Export the sessions whose pinned terms admit the purpose, redacted under
108	   * one profile, and write the manifest that accounts for every session the
109	   * request considered.
110	   * @param request - the purpose, the profile, the sessions, the sink, and the exporter's own filters.
111	   * @returns the manifest with the counts behind it, including the sessions withheld by terms and the ones that could not be read.
112	   * @throws {@link CuratorError} `CURATOR_PROFILE_REQUIRED` when neither the
113	   *   request nor the configuration names a profile, and `CURATOR_PROFILE_UNKNOWN`
114	   *   when the request names one this deployment did not configure. Nothing is
115	   *   written and the sink is not touched in either case.
116	   */
117	  async export(request: CuratedExportRequest): Promise<CuratedExportReport> {
118	    const profile = this.resolveProfile(request.profile)
119	    const skipped: TrajectoryExportSkip[] = []
120	    const admitted = new Map<SessionId, DataUseTerms>()
121	    let withheldByTerms = 0
122	    const candidates = request.sessions ?? (await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.list()).map(header => header.id)
123	    for (const sessionId of candidates) {
124	      let terms: DataUseTerms | undefined
125	      try {
126	        terms = termsOf((await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect(sessionId)).events)
127	      } catch (error: unknown) {
128	        skipped.push({ sessionId, reason: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
129	        continue
130	      }
131	      // No terms, no export: an unpinned transcript states no purpose, and a
132	      // purpose nobody recorded is never assumed.
133	      if (terms === undefined || !terms.purposes.includes(request.purpose)) {
134	        withheldByTerms += 1
135	        continue
136	      }
137	      admitted.set(sessionId, terms)
138	    }
139	
140	    const ruleHits = new Map<string, number>()
141	    const records = createHash('sha256')
142	    const report = await this.ctx.trajectories.export({
143	      sessions: [...admitted.keys()],
144	      sink: {
145	        write: async (line) => {
146	          const curated = this.curate(JSON.parse(line) as Trajectory, profile, admitted, ruleHits)
147	          records.update(curated)
148	          await request.sink.write(curated)
149	        },
150	        close: () => request.sink.close(),
151	      },
152	      ...request.rewardedOnly === undefined ? {} : { rewardedOnly: request.rewardedOnly },
153	      ...request.includeHeldOut === undefined ? {} : { includeHeldOut: request.includeHeldOut },
154	      ...request.districts === undefined ? {} : { districts: request.districts },
155	    })
156	
157	    const manifest: ExportManifest = {
158	      version: EXPORT_MANIFEST_VERSION,
159	      exportedAt: Date.now(),
160	      purpose: request.purpose,
161	      profile: profile.id,
162	      profileSha256: profile.sha256,
163	      records: report.exported,
164	      withheld: { heldOut: report.heldOut, districts: report.withheld, terms: withheldByTerms },
165	      // Every rule of the profile is listed, so a reviewer reading the manifest
166	      // sees which rules never fired at all.
167	      ruleHits: Object.fromEntries(profile.rules.map(rule => [rule.id, ruleHits.get(rule.id) ?? 0])),
168	      recordsSha256: records.digest('hex'),
169	      trajectoryFormat: TRAJECTORY_FORMAT,
170	    }
171	    if (request.manifestPath !== undefined) await writeFile(request.manifestPath, `${JSON.stringify(manifest, undefined, 2)}\n`)
172	    return {
173	      manifest,
174	      sessions: candidates.length,
175	      exported: report.exported,
176	      rewarded: report.rewarded,
177	      filtered: report.filtered,
178	      heldOut: report.heldOut,
179	      withheldByDistrict: report.withheld,
180	      withheldByTerms,
181	      skipped: [...skipped, ...report.skipped],
182	    }
183	  }
184	
185	  /**
186	   * The profile one export runs under.
187	   * @param requested - the profile the request named, if any.
188	   * @returns the compiled profile.
189	   * @throws {@link CuratorError} when no profile is named or the named one is unknown.
190	   */
191	  private resolveProfile(requested: string | undefined): RedactionProfile {
192	    const id = requested ?? this.defaultProfile
193	    if (id === undefined) {
194	      throw new CuratorError(
195	        'this export names no redaction profile and no defaultProfile is configured; a curated export never runs unredacted',
196	        'CURATOR_PROFILE_REQUIRED',
197	      )
198	    }
199	    const profile = this.profiles.get(id)
200	    if (profile === undefined) {
201	      throw new CuratorError(
202	        `redaction profile "${id}" is not configured; this deployment configured ${[...this.profiles.keys()].join(', ')}`,
203	        'CURATOR_PROFILE_UNKNOWN',
204	      )
205	    }
206	    return profile
207	  }
208	
209	  /**
210	   * Redact one folded record and attach the curation block the export states.
211	   * @param record - the record the exporter serialized.
212	   * @param profile - the profile this export runs under.
213	   * @param admitted - the terms of every session the terms pass admitted.
214	   * @param ruleHits - export-wide replacement counts, incremented in place.
215	   * @returns the curated line, newline included.
216	   * @throws {@link CuratorError} when the record names a session the terms pass did not admit.
217	   */
218	  private curate(
219	    record: Trajectory,
220	    profile: RedactionProfile,
221	    admitted: ReadonlyMap<SessionId, DataUseTerms>,
222	    ruleHits: Map<string, number>,
223	  ): string {
224	    const terms = admitted.get(record.id)
225	    /* v8 ignore next 4 -- the exporter reads only the sessions the terms pass admitted and mapped. */
226	    if (terms === undefined) {
227	      throw new CuratorError(
228	        `session ${record.id} reached the sink without admitted terms`,
229	        'CURATOR_UNADMITTED_RECORD',
230	      )
231	    }
232	    const hits = new Map<string, number>()
233	    const redacted = redactTrajectory(record, profile.rules, hits)
234	    for (const [id, count] of hits) ruleHits.set(id, (ruleHits.get(id) ?? 0) + count)
235	    const curated: CuratedTrajectory = {
236	      ...redacted,
237	      curation: {
238	        redactionApplied: true,
239	        redaction: { profile: profile.id, profileSha256: profile.sha256, hits: Object.fromEntries(hits) },
240	        residency: terms.residency,
241	      },
242	    }
243	    return `${JSON.stringify(curated)}\n`
244	  }
245	}
246	
247	export default CuratorService

1	/**
2	 * Redaction profiles and the walk that applies one to a trajectory record: the
3	 * rule set this package ships, the load-time compilation every configured rule
4	 * passes, and the enumeration of what a record never has redacted.
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-curator
6	 */
7	
8	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
9	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
10	import type { Trajectory } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories/types'
11	import type { RedactionProfileConfig, RedactionRule } from './types.ts'
12	
13	/** Stable error codes of a refused profile or a refused export. */
14	export type CuratorErrorCode =
15	  | 'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG'
16	  | 'CURATOR_PROFILE_REQUIRED'
17	  | 'CURATOR_PROFILE_UNKNOWN'
18	  | 'CURATOR_UNADMITTED_RECORD'
19	
20	/** Error raised by a profile the curator cannot compile or an export it refuses to run. */
21	export class CuratorError extends HarnessError {
22	  /**
23	   * @param message - human-readable reason, naming the profile or rule at fault.
24	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
25	   */
26	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
27	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
28	  constructor(message: string, code: CuratorErrorCode) {
29	    super(message, code)

33	/**
34	 * The rules this package owns, applied ahead of a profile's own when it sets
35	 * `shipped: true`. Each covers one credential or identifier format that turns
36	 * up verbatim in agent transcripts; none of them claims to be exhaustive, and a
37	 * deployment adds its own formats through `rules`.

39	export const SHIPPED_REDACTION_RULES: readonly RedactionRule[] = [
40	  {
41	    id: 'shipped:email',
42	    pattern: String.raw`[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}`,
43	    flags: 'g',
44	    replacement: '[redacted:email]',
45	  },
46	  {
47	    id: 'shipped:bearer-token',
48	    // Twenty characters keeps the prose "Bearer token" out of the rule while
49	    // matching every credential an Authorization header actually carries.
50	    pattern: String.raw`\bBearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/-]{20,}=*`,
51	    flags: 'gi',
52	    replacement: 'Bearer [redacted:token]',
53	  },
54	  {

56	    pattern: String.raw`\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{4,}\b`,

63	    flags: 'g',

74	/**
75	 * Record subtrees that carry only identifiers, digests, counts, and closed
76	 * vocabularies. Nothing under `terms` (the agreement and the purposes it
77	 * admits), `environment` (the `environment/run` stamp), `steps`, `parity`, or
78	 * `provenance` is free text, and redacting one of them would break the keys a
79	 * scoreboard and a decontamination check are computed from, or the terms a
80	 * later consumer re-checks this export's purpose against.

84	/**
85	 * Key names that hold an identifier or a closed vocabulary wherever they appear
86	 * in the record. A rule that rewrote one of these would corrupt a value the
87	 * record's readers switch on rather than protect anything the record carries.
88	 */
89	const NEVER_REDACTED_KEYS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
90	  'format',
91	  'type',
92	  'id',
93	  'sessionId',
94	  'parentSession',
95	  'agentPreset',
96	  'role',
97	  'sourceKind',
98	  'toolCallId',
99	  'basis',
100	  'phase',
101	  'goalId',
102	  'checkId',
103	  'status',
104	  'isolation',
105	  'executor',
106	  'provider',
107	  'model',
108	  'reasoningEffort',
109	  'attachmentId',
110	  'mediaType',
111	])

113	/**
114	 * Paths whose `name` is a registered tool name rather than free text. The key
115	 * alone cannot decide it: an attachment's `name` is a display filename and is
116	 * redacted like any other text a person supplied.

118	const NEVER_REDACTED_PATHS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
119	  'tools.name',
120	  'messages.content.name',
121	  'messages.toolCalls.name',
122	])
123	
124	/** Where one string sits in the record; array indices are elided, so every element of a list shares its path. */
125	interface RedactionSite {
126	  /** Top-level record key the string descends from. */
127	  readonly root: string
128	  /** Dotted path from the record root, indices elided. */
129	  readonly path: string
130	  /** Key the string is stored under. */
131	  readonly key: string

133	
134	/** One rule ready to run, with the regular expression the load compiled. */
135	export interface CompiledRedactionRule {
136	  /** The configured rule id, which hit counts are reported under. */
137	  readonly id: string
138	  /** The compiled pattern, always global so every hit is replaced and counted. */
139	  readonly regex: RegExp
140	  /** Literal replacement text. */
141	  readonly replacement: string
142	}
143	
144	/** A profile as the service holds it: its rules in run order and the digest that addresses them. */
145	export interface RedactionProfile {
146	  /** Configured profile id. */
147	  readonly id: string
148	  /** Shipped rules first when the profile asked for them, then the configured ones. */
149	  readonly rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[]
150	  /** Lowercase SHA-256 hex over the rules' sources, flags, and replacements in order. */
151	  readonly sha256: string
152	}
153	
154	/**
155	 * Compile one configured profile, refusing every rule a load may not accept.
156	 * @param id - the profile id, named in every rejection.
157	 * @param config - the profile's shipped-rule choice and its own rules.
158	 * @returns the compiled profile with its digest.
159	 * @throws {@link CuratorError} `CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG` when the profile holds
160	 *   no rule, or when a rule has an empty id, an id another rule in the same
161	 *   profile already used, the sticky flag, or a pattern that does not compile.
162	 */
163	export function compileProfile(id: string, config: RedactionProfileConfig): RedactionProfile {
164	  const rules = [...config.shipped ? SHIPPED_REDACTION_RULES : [], ...config.rules ?? []]
165	  if (rules.length === 0) {
166	    throw new CuratorError(
167	      `redaction profile "${id}" lists no rule and does not take the shipped set, so it would redact nothing`,
168	      'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG',
169	    )
170	  }
171	  const seen = new Set<string>()
172	  const compiled = rules.map((rule) => {
173	    if (rule.id.length === 0) throw new CuratorError(`redaction profile "${id}" has a rule with an empty id`, 'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG')
174	    if (seen.has(rule.id)) {
175	      throw new CuratorError(`redaction profile "${id}" lists rule "${rule.id}" twice, so its hit count would name two rules`, 'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG')
176	    }
177	    seen.add(rule.id)
178	    return { id: rule.id, regex: compileRule(id, rule), replacement: rule.replacement }
179	  })
180	  return { id, rules: compiled, sha256: profileDigest(compiled) }
181	}
182	
183	/**
184	 * Compile one rule's pattern, always globally.
185	 * @param profileId - owning profile, named in a rejection.
186	 * @param rule - the configured rule.
187	 * @returns the compiled expression.
188	 * @throws {@link CuratorError} on the sticky flag or an uncompilable pattern.
189	 */
190	function compileRule(profileId: string, rule: RedactionRule): RegExp {
191	  const flags = rule.flags ?? ''
192	  if (flags.includes('y')) {
193	    throw new CuratorError(
194	      `redaction rule "${rule.id}" of profile "${profileId}" sets the sticky flag, which would match only at the expression's last index and leave later hits in the record`,
195	      'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG',
196	    )
197	  }
198	  try {
199	    return new RegExp(rule.pattern, flags.includes('g') ? flags : `${flags}g`)
200	  } catch (error: unknown) {
201	    // The RegExp constructor is the only thrower here and it throws a SyntaxError.
202	    throw new CuratorError(`redaction rule "${rule.id}" of profile "${profileId}" does not compile: ${String(error)}`, 'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG')
203	  }
204	}
205	
206	/**
207	 * Digest the rules that will actually run, so a manifest states which rules a
208	 * profile name stood for rather than only the name.
209	 * @param rules - the compiled rules in run order.
210	 * @returns lowercase SHA-256 hex over their canonical encoding.
211	 */
212	function profileDigest(rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[]): string {
213	  const canonical = rules.map(rule => ({
214	    id: rule.id,
215	    source: rule.regex.source,
216	    flags: rule.regex.flags,
217	    replacement: rule.replacement,
218	  }))
219	  return createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(canonical)).digest('hex')
220	}
221	
222	/**
223	 * Replace every match of every rule, in rule order, counting the replacements.
224	 * The replacement is returned from a function, so a `$&` or `$1` a deployment
225	 * configured is written literally and can never splice the matched text back in.
226	 * @param text - the string to redact.
227	 * @param rules - the profile's rules in run order.
228	 * @param hits - replacement counts per rule id, incremented in place.
229	 * @returns the redacted string.
230	 */
231	export function applyRules(text: string, rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[], hits: Map<string, number>): string {
232	  let redacted = text
233	  for (const rule of rules) {
234	    redacted = redacted.replace(rule.regex, () => {
235	      hits.set(rule.id, (hits.get(rule.id) ?? 0) + 1)
236	      return rule.replacement
237	    })
238	  }
239	  return redacted
240	}
241	
242	/**
243	 * Whether one string keeps its exact value.
244	 * @param site - where the string sits in the record.
245	 * @returns true for the record's identifiers, discriminants, and tool names.
246	 */
247	function keeps(site: RedactionSite): boolean {
248	  return NEVER_REDACTED_SUBTREES.has(site.root)
249	    || NEVER_REDACTED_KEYS.has(site.key)
250	    || NEVER_REDACTED_PATHS.has(site.path)
251	}
252	
253	/**
254	 * Redact one value and everything under it.
255	 * @param value - the value at `site`.
256	 * @param site - where the value sits in the record.
257	 * @param rules - the profile's rules in run order.
258	 * @param hits - replacement counts per rule id, incremented in place.
259	 * @returns the value with every redacted string replaced.
260	 */
261	function redactValue(value: unknown, site: RedactionSite, rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[], hits: Map<string, number>): unknown {
262	  if (typeof value === 'string') return keeps(site) ? value : applyRules(value, rules, hits)
263	  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(item => redactValue(item, site, rules, hits))
264	  if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null) return redactEntries(value, site, rules, hits)
265	  return value
266	}
267	
268	/**
269	 * Redact every property of one object, descending with the property's path.
270	 * @param value - the object to walk.
271	 * @param site - where the object sits, or `undefined` at the record root.
272	 * @param rules - the profile's rules in run order.
273	 * @param hits - replacement counts per rule id, incremented in place.
274	 * @returns a new object with the same keys.
275	 */
276	function redactEntries(
277	  value: object,
278	  site: RedactionSite | undefined,
279	  rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[],
280	  hits: Map<string, number>,
281	): Record<string, unknown> {
282	  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(value).map(([key, entry]) => [
283	    key,
284	    redactValue(entry, site === undefined ? { root: key, path: key, key } : { root: site.root, path: `${site.path}.${key}`, key }, rules, hits),
285	  ]))
286	}
287	
288	/**
289	 * Apply a profile to one trajectory record. Every string is redacted except the
290	 * record's identifiers, its readers' discriminants, and registered tool names,
291	 * so a field added to the record format is redacted until someone decides
292	 * otherwise rather than exported until someone notices.
293	 * @param record - the folded record, as the exporter serialized it.
294	 * @param rules - the profile's rules in run order.
295	 * @param hits - replacement counts per rule id, incremented in place.
296	 * @returns a new record with the same keys and every redacted string replaced.
297	 */
298	export function redactTrajectory(record: Trajectory, rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[], hits: Map<string, number>): Trajectory {
299	  // The walk replaces string leaves and preserves every key, so the result is
300	  // the same record format with redacted text.
301	  return redactEntries(record, undefined, rules, hits) as unknown as Trajectory
302	}

1	/**
2	 * Trajectory export: persisted sessions folded into `dsh-trajectory/2`
3	 * records and written one JSON line at a time to a caller-supplied sink. The
4	 * service reads through the session persistence seam and writes no session
5	 * event. The
6	 * [trajectory-export Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md)
7	 * owns the design rationale.
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories
9	 */
10	
11	import { open } from 'node:fs/promises'
12	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
13	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
14	// Type-only: resolves ctx.sessionPersistence.
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
16	import { foldTrajectory } from './fold.ts'
17	import type {
18	  TrajectoryExportReport,
19	  TrajectoryExportRequest,
20	  TrajectoryExportSkip,
21	  TrajectorySink,
22	} from './types.ts'
23	
24	export type * from './types.ts'
25	export { foldTrajectory, foldTrajectoryReward, TRAJECTORY_FORMAT } from './fold.ts'
26	
27	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
28	  interface Context {
29	    trajectories: TrajectoryService
30	  }
31	}
32	
33	/** Deployment choices of the exporter, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
34	export interface Config {
35	  /**
36	   * Districts an export that names none withholds, counted as `withheld`. The
37	   * package ships no district name: a deployment states the districts whose
38	   * sessions may not leave it by default.
39	   */
40	  withheldDistricts?: string[]
41	}
42	
43	/** The exporter's choices with every default applied. */
44	export interface ResolvedConfig {
45	  readonly withheldDistricts: readonly string[]
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * Apply the exporter's defaults to a validated config.
50	 * @param config - validated deployment config.
51	 * @returns the resolved choices: no district withheld unless configured.
52	 */
53	export function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
54	  return { withheldDistricts: config.withheldDistricts ?? [] }
55	}
56	
57	/** Render a read or fold failure for the export report without trusting the thrown value. */
58	function reasonOf(error: unknown): string {
59	  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
60	}
61	
62	/**
63	 * A sink that appends lines to one file, created or truncated on first use.
64	 * @param path - destination file path.
65	 * @returns a sink the exporter closes when the export settles.
66	 */
67	export function jsonlFileSink(path: string): TrajectorySink {
68	  const handle = open(path, 'w')
69	  return {
70	    async write(line) {
71	      await (await handle).write(line)
72	    },
73	    async close() {
74	      await (await handle).close()
75	    },
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	/** Trajectory exporter (`ctx.trajectories`): persisted sessions as training and evaluation records. */
80	export class TrajectoryService extends Service {
81	  static inject = ['sessionPersistence']
82	
83	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
84	    withheldDistricts: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
85	  })
86	
87	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
88	
89	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config = {}) {
90	    super(ctx, 'trajectories')
91	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
92	  }
93	
94	  /**
95	   * Fold the requested sessions and write one line per trajectory. A session
96	   * that cannot be read or folded is reported and the export continues; the
97	   * sink is closed exactly once when every session has been handled.
98	   * @param request - sessions to export, the destination sink, the reward filter, the held-out opt-in, and the districts to write.
99	   * @returns counts of sessions, written lines, rewarded lines, filtered
100	   *   sessions, withheld held-out and district sessions, and skips with reasons.
101	   */
102	  async export(request: TrajectoryExportRequest): Promise<TrajectoryExportReport> {
103	    const persistence = this.ctx.sessionPersistence
104	    const sessions = request.sessions ?? (await persistence.list()).map(header => header.id)
105	    const skipped: TrajectoryExportSkip[] = []
106	    let exported = 0
107	    let rewarded = 0
108	    let filtered = 0
109	    let heldOut = 0
110	    let withheld = 0
111	    try {
112	      for (const sessionId of sessions) {
113	        let line: string
114	        let outcome: 1 | 0 | null
115	        let reserved: boolean
116	        let district: string | undefined
117	        try {
118	          const { meta, events } = await persistence.inspect(sessionId)
119	          const trajectory = foldTrajectory(meta, events)
120	          outcome = trajectory.reward.outcome
121	          reserved = trajectory.environment?.heldOut === true
122	          district = trajectory.environment?.district
123	          line = `${JSON.stringify(trajectory)}\n`
124	        } catch (error: unknown) {
125	          skipped.push({ sessionId, reason: reasonOf(error) })
126	          continue
127	        }
128	        if (reserved && request.includeHeldOut !== true) {
129	          heldOut += 1
130	          continue
131	        }
132	        if (this.withholds(district, request.districts)) {
133	          withheld += 1
134	          continue
135	        }
136	        if (request.rewardedOnly === true && outcome !== 1) {
137	          filtered += 1
138	          continue
139	        }
140	        await request.sink.write(line)
141	        exported += 1
142	        if (outcome === 1) rewarded += 1
143	      }
144	    } finally {
145	      await request.sink.close()
146	    }
147	    return { sessions: sessions.length, exported, rewarded, filtered, heldOut, withheld, skipped }
148	  }
149	
150	  /**
151	   * Whether a session's district keeps it out of this export: a request that
152	   * names districts writes exactly those, and one that names none withholds
153	   * the configured districts.
154	   */
155	  private withholds(district: string | undefined, districts: readonly string[] | undefined): boolean {
156	    if (districts !== undefined) return district === undefined || !districts.includes(district)
157	    return district !== undefined && this.resolved.withheldDistricts.includes(district)
158	  }
159	}
160	
161	export default TrajectoryService

53	    type: 'session',

65	
66	/**
67	 * Parse a header line back into a {@link SessionHeader}.
68	 * @param line - the shape-checked first line of a log (see the `isHeaderLine` guard).
69	 * @returns the header, absent optional fields omitted.
70	 */
71	export function fromHeaderLine(line: HeaderLine): SessionHeader {
72	  if (Object.hasOwn(line, 'sandboxMode') || Object.hasOwn(line, 'approvalPolicy')) {
73	    throw new Error('session header uses retired policy baseline fields')
74	  }
75	  return {
76	    version: line.version,
77	    id: line.id,
78	    createdAt: line.createdAt,
79	    ...line.cwd !== undefined ? { cwd: line.cwd } : {},
80	    ...line.parentSession !== undefined ? { parentSession: line.parentSession } : {},
81	    ...line.seedLength !== undefined ? { seedLength: line.seedLength } : {},
82	    ...line.origin !== undefined ? { origin: line.origin } : {},
83	    delegationDepth: line.delegationDepth,
84	    ...line.agentPreset !== undefined ? { agentPreset: line.agentPreset } : {},
85	  }
86	}
87	
88	/** Type guard: a parsed first line is a well-formed session header. */
89	function isHeaderLine(value: unknown): value is HeaderLine {
90	  return (
91	    typeof value === 'object' && value !== null
92	    && (value as { type?: unknown }).type === 'session'
93	    && typeof (value as { version?: unknown }).version === 'number'
94	    && typeof (value as { id?: unknown }).id === 'string'
95	    && typeof (value as { createdAt?: unknown }).createdAt === 'number'
96	    && Number.isSafeInteger((value as { createdAt: number }).createdAt)
97	    && (value as { createdAt: number }).createdAt >= 0
98	    && !Object.is((value as { createdAt: number }).createdAt, -0)
99	    && typeof (value as { delegationDepth?: unknown }).delegationDepth === 'number'
100	    && Number.isSafeInteger((value as { delegationDepth: number }).delegationDepth)
101	    && (value as { delegationDepth: number }).delegationDepth >= 0
102	    && !Object.is((value as { delegationDepth: number }).delegationDepth, -0)
103	    && ((value as { origin?: unknown }).origin === undefined
104	      || (value as { origin?: unknown }).origin === 'subagent')
105	    && ((value as { agentPreset?: unknown }).agentPreset === undefined
106	      || typeof (value as { agentPreset?: unknown }).agentPreset === 'string')
107	  )
108	}
109	
110	/**
111	 * Encode an arbitrary string as a single safe path segment, injectively over ALL JS (UTF-16)
112	 * strings — including lone surrogates. A {@link SessionId} is an unvalidated branded string,
113	 * so this neutralizes `../`, absolute paths, NUL, and separators before any filesystem use.
114	 * Safe code units remain literal; every other unit, including `~`, becomes
115	 * `~XXXX`. Operating on code units preserves lone surrogates, while special-
116	 * casing `.` and `..` prevents traversal by an otherwise safe whole segment.
117	 *
118	 * @param raw - the string to encode; must be non-empty (throws on `''`).
119	 * @returns the escaped single path segment, decodable back to `raw`.
120	 */
121	export function encodeSegment(raw: string): string {
122	  if (raw.length === 0) throw new Error('cannot encode an empty path segment')
123	  if (raw === '.') return '~002E'
124	  if (raw === '..') return '~002E~002E'
125	  let out = ''
126	  for (let i = 0; i < raw.length; i++) {
127	    const code = raw.charCodeAt(i)
128	    const ch = String.fromCharCode(code)
129	    if (ch !== '~' && /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]$/.test(ch)) {
130	      out += ch
131	    } else {
132	      out += '~' + code.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(4, '0')
133	    }
134	  }
135	  return out
136	}
137	
138	/**
139	 * Build the readable directory key for a project path.
140	 * Filesystem separators and drive separators become `-`; unsafe code units use
141	 * the same `~XXXX` escape as session ids. The key is bounded for filesystem
142	 * component limits. Separator replacement and truncation are intentionally
143	 * lossy, following the common human-navigable project-directory convention.
144	 * @param cwd - the session's project directory.
145	 * @returns a single filesystem-safe project directory name.
146	 */
147	export function projectKey(cwd: string): string {
148	  if (cwd.length === 0) throw new Error('cannot encode an empty project path')
149	  let readable = ''
150	  let separatorRun = false
151	  for (let i = 0; i < cwd.length; i++) {
152	    const code = cwd.charCodeAt(i)
153	    const ch = String.fromCharCode(code)
154	    if (ch === '/' || ch === '\\' || ch === ':') {
155	      if (!separatorRun) readable += '-'
156	      separatorRun = true
157	    } else if (ch !== '~' && /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]$/.test(ch)) {
158	      readable += ch
159	      separatorRun = false
160	    } else {
161	      readable += '~' + code.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(4, '0')
162	      separatorRun = false
163	    }
164	  }
165	  const slug = readable.replace(/^-+/, '') || 'root'
166	  return `--${slug.slice(0, 251)}--`
167	}
168	
169	/**
170	 * The configured root's human-navigable project directory. A configured root
171	 * may be local or shared; this grouping does not prescribe its deployment.
172	 * @param root - the backend's session root directory.
173	 * @param cwd - the session's project directory; `undefined` selects `_no-cwd`.
174	 * @returns the project directory path under `root`.
175	 */
176	export function projectDir(root: string, cwd: string | undefined): string {
177	  if (cwd === undefined) return join(root, '_no-cwd')
178	  return join(root, projectKey(cwd))
179	}
180	
181	/**
182	 * The directory owned by one session and available for future session-local
183	 * artifacts.
184	 * @param root - the backend's session root directory.
185	 * @param cwd - the session's project directory.
186	 * @param id - the session id, encoded to one safe path segment.
187	 * @returns the session directory beneath its project directory.
188	 */
189	export function sessionDir(root: string, cwd: string | undefined, id: SessionId): string {
190	  return join(projectDir(root, cwd), encodeSegment(id))
191	}
192	
193	/**
194	 * The append-only event-log file path for a session.
195	 * @param root - the backend's session root directory.
196	 * @param cwd - the session's project directory (`undefined` → `_no-cwd`).
197	 * @param id - the session id, path-encoded via {@link encodeSegment} before filesystem use.
198	 * @param compression - physical artifact encoding and filename suffix.
199	 * @returns the session's configured JSONL artifact path.
200	 */
201	export function logPath(
202	  root: string,
203	  cwd: string | undefined,
204	  id: SessionId,
205	  compression: JsonlCompression,
206	): string {
207	  return join(sessionDir(root, cwd, id), `session${logSuffix(compression)}`)
208	}
209	
210	/**
211	 * Serialize an event batch as JSONL lines (no trailing newline). With
212	 * `packChunks` on, delta-chunk runs pack into `text-chunks` /
213	 * `reasoning-chunks` / `tool-call-chunks` storage rows; off writes one event
214	 * per line, byte-identical to the pre-packing layout. Reading is layout-blind
215	 * either way ({@link scanLog} always decodes rows), so the switch changes only
216	 * newly written bytes.
217	 * @param events - the batch to serialize, in log order.
218	 * @param packChunks - whether to pack delta runs into storage rows.
219	 * @returns the batch's JSONL text; the writer adds the final newline.
220	 */
221	export function eventLines(events: readonly SessionEvent[], packChunks: boolean): string {
222	  const records: readonly StorageRecord[] = packChunks ? packChunkRuns(events) : events
223	  return records.map(record => JSON.stringify(record)).join('\n')
224	}
225	
226	interface SessionLogScan {
227	  meta: SessionHeader
228	  events: SessionEvent[]
229	  committedBytes: number
230	}
231	
232	/** Parse one complete header record supplied independently from event rows. */
233	/**
234	 * Refuse a header carrying a format version this build does not read BEFORE
235	 * validating the current header shape or decoding any event row: a future
236	 * format need not satisfy today's structural checks at all, and its user must
237	 * see "upgrade the harness", never "corrupt session log".
238	 * @param parsed - the JSON-parsed first line of a session artifact.
239	 */
240	function refuseForeignFormatVersion(parsed: unknown): void {
241	  if (typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null) return
242	  const { version, id } = parsed as { version?: unknown; id?: unknown }
243	  if (typeof version !== 'number' || version === SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION) return
244	  throw new SessionFormatUnsupportedError(
245	    sessionFormatVersionRefusal(typeof id === 'string' ? id : String(id), version),
246	  )
247	}
248	
249	function parseHeaderRecord(record: Buffer): SessionHeader {
250	  if (record.length === 0 || record.at(-1) !== 0x0A || record.indexOf(0x0A) !== record.length - 1) {
251	    throw new Error('empty or header-less session log')
252	  }
253	  let parsed: unknown
254	  try {
255	    parsed = JSON.parse(record.subarray(0, -1).toString('utf8'))
256	  } catch {
257	    throw new Error('corrupt session log: header line is not valid JSON')
258	  }
259	  refuseForeignFormatVersion(parsed)
260	  if (!isHeaderLine(parsed)) {
261	    throw new Error('corrupt session log: first line is not a session header')
262	  }
263	  return fromHeaderLine(parsed)
264	}
265	
266	/**
267	 * Incrementally scan complete JSONL event records after an independently
268	 * supplied header record. Newline search and byte offsets stay on raw buffers;
269	 * only complete records are decoded to UTF-8. A fragment crossing writes is
270	 * copied because a decoder may reuse its output buffer after `write()` returns.
271	 */
272	export class SessionLogScanner {
273	  private readonly meta: SessionHeader
274	  private readonly events: SessionEvent[] = []
275	  private fragments: Buffer[] = []
276	  private fragmentBytes = 0
277	  private inputBytes: number
278	  private committedBytes: number
279	  private eventLine = 0
280	  private issue: Error | undefined
281	  private finished = false
282	
283	  /**
284	   * Create an event scanner from exactly one newline-terminated header record.
285	   * @param headerRecord - the complete first JSONL record, including its newline.
286	   */
287	  constructor(headerRecord: Buffer) {
288	    this.meta = parseHeaderRecord(headerRecord)
289	    this.inputBytes = headerRecord.length
290	    this.committedBytes = headerRecord.length
291	  }
292	
293	  /**
294	   * Consume the next raw plaintext chunk, retaining only an incomplete final record.
295	   * @param chunk - bytes immediately following all previously supplied bytes.
296	   */
297	  write(chunk: Buffer): void {
298	    if (this.finished) throw new Error('cannot write to a finished session log scanner')
299	    const chunkStart = this.inputBytes
300	    this.inputBytes += chunk.length
301	    let lineStart = 0
302	    for (
303	      let newline = chunk.indexOf(0x0A);
304	      newline !== -1;
305	      newline = chunk.indexOf(0x0A, lineStart)
306	    ) {
307	      const fragment = chunk.subarray(lineStart, newline)
308	      let line = fragment
309	      if (this.fragments.length > 0) {
310	        if (fragment.length > 0) this.fragments.push(fragment)
311	        line = Buffer.concat(this.fragments, this.fragmentBytes + fragment.length)
312	        this.fragments = []
313	        this.fragmentBytes = 0
314	      }
315	      this.consumeEventLine(line, chunkStart + newline + 1)
316	      lineStart = newline + 1
317	    }
318	    if (lineStart < chunk.length) {
319	      const fragment = Buffer.from(chunk.subarray(lineStart))
320	      this.fragments.push(fragment)
321	      this.fragmentBytes += fragment.length
322	    }
323	  }
324	
325	  /**
326	   * Snapshot progress before appending a recoverable torn-frame prefix.
327	   * @returns byte, committed-prefix, and expanded-event cursors.
328	   */
329	  checkpoint(): { inputBytes: number; committedBytes: number; eventCount: number } {
330	    return {
331	      inputBytes: this.inputBytes,
332	      committedBytes: this.committedBytes,
333	      eventCount: this.events.length,
334	    }
335	  }
336	
337	  /**
338	   * Finish scanning, ignoring a final record without a newline as a torn tail.
339	   * @returns the header, contiguous event prefix, and safe truncation offset.
340	   */
341	  finish(): SessionLogScan {
342	    this.finished = true
343	    return { meta: this.meta, events: this.events, committedBytes: this.committedBytes }
344	  }
345	
346	  /** Decode one complete event row and update the contiguous prefix. */
347	  private consumeEventLine(line: Buffer, endByte: number): void {
348	    this.eventLine += 1
349	    let decoded: SessionEvent[]
350	    try {
351	      decoded = decodeStorageRecord(JSON.parse(line.toString('utf8')))
352	    } catch {
353	      this.issue ??= new Error(`corrupt session log: unparsable committed event at line ${this.eventLine}`)
354	      return
355	    }
356	
357	    if (this.issue !== undefined) {
358	      if (decoded.some(event => event.type === 'turn/end')) throw this.issue
359	      return
360	    }
361	
362	    const rowStart = this.events.length
363	    for (const event of decoded) {
364	      if (event.seq !== this.events.length) {
365	        const expected = this.events.length
366	        this.events.length = rowStart
367	        this.issue = new Error(
368	          `corrupt session log: seq gap in committed region at line ${this.eventLine} `
369	          + `(expected ${expected}, got ${event.seq})`,
370	        )
371	        if (decoded.some(candidate => candidate.type === 'turn/end')) throw this.issue
372	        return
373	      }
374	      this.events.push(event)
375	    }
376	    this.committedBytes = endByte
377	  }
378	}
379	
380	/**
381	 * Parse a complete or torn JSONL buffer into its preserved event prefix. This
382	 * compatibility wrapper supplies the first record separately, then delegates
383	 * event rows to {@link SessionLogScanner}.
384	 *
385	 * @param buffer - the raw bytes of the log file (header line first).
386	 * @returns the header, preserved event prefix, and byte offset safe to append at.
387	 */
388	export function scanLog(buffer: Buffer): SessionLogScan {
389	  const headerEnd = buffer.indexOf(0x0A)
390	  if (headerEnd === -1) throw new Error('empty or header-less session log')
391	  const scanner = new SessionLogScanner(buffer.subarray(0, headerEnd + 1))
392	  scanner.write(buffer.subarray(headerEnd + 1))
393	  return scanner.finish()
394	}
395	
396	/**
397	 * Parse just the header line of a log into a {@link SessionHeader}, or
398	 * `undefined` if it is missing/not a header. Used by `list()` to read session
399	 * metadata WITHOUT parsing the whole log: a session picker scales with the
400	 * number of sessions, not the total size of every conversation.
401	 * @param firstLine - the first line of a log file (without its trailing newline).
402	 * @returns the parsed header, or `undefined` when the line is not a well-formed session header.
403	 */
404	export function parseHeaderMeta(firstLine: string): SessionHeader | undefined {
405	  let parsed: unknown
406	  try {
407	    parsed = JSON.parse(firstLine)
408	  } catch {
409	    return undefined
410	  }
411	  if (!isHeaderLine(parsed)) return undefined
412	  return fromHeaderLine(parsed)
413	}
